If no, was it made by the manager for legal necessity or the benefit of the estate, with necessity or proper inquiry proved by the alienee? If yes, it binds adults and minors. If no, was it made by the father to pay his own antecedent debt, not immoral or illegal? If no, it is voidable at the option of the other coparceners and binds only the alienor's own interest where the school allows. If yes, was the debt contracted before 9 September 2005? If yes, it binds the sons' interest. If no, Section 6(4) applies and pious obligation alone cannot bind the sons' interest.
keyPoints: Only all adult coparceners, the manager, the father and a sole surviving coparcener can alienate so as to bind the family (Mulla, section 255). The manager may alienate only for legal necessity or benefit of the estate ( Brij Narain , para 17(1); Mulla, section 242). The buyer or lender must prove necessity or proper honest inquiry; he need not see to the use of the money (section 244). An alienation without necessity is voidable, not void (section 242(4)). The father may bind the estate for his own antecedent, non-immoral debt; antecedent means in time and in fact ( Brij Narain , para 17). Section 6(4) ends pious obligation as the sole ground for debts after 9 September 2005. A gift of an undivided interest is void; a sale for value is allowed in Bombay, Madras and Madhya Pradesh (sections 258–260). Damdupat: interest recoverable at one time cannot exceed the principal (section 596).

caseLaws.name: Brij Narain v
caseLaws.facts: Mangla Prasad (1923) Facts. In 1908 Sita Ram, manager of a joint family with his two minor sons, mortgaged ancestral property for Rs. 11,000 to pay off two earlier mortgages of 1905 and 1907. The sons, through their mother, sued to have it declared not binding on them. Principle. The five propositions in para 17: the manager binds the estate only for necessity; a father may lay it open to execution for a non-immoral debt; his mortgage binds only if it discharges an antecedent debt, antecedent in time and in fact; and it makes no difference whether he is alive or dead. The older mortgages were antecedent debts, so the 1908 mortgage bound the estate and the appeal was allowed (paras 18–19). Privy Council, (1924) 26 Bom LR 500 : (1924) 51 IA 129. Why it matters. It is the leading statement of the father's power over joint family property for his own debts. Hunoomanpersaud Panday v. Mussumat Babooee Munraj Koonweree (1856) Facts. A mother, managing her minor son's estate, mortgaged it (as described in Mulla, section 242). Principle. The manager's power "can only be exercised rightly in a case of need, or for the benefit of the estate"; a lender must inquire, and if he acts honestly after inquiry, the actual existence of the necessity is not a condition of his charge (quoted in Mulla, section 242). (1856) 6 Moo IA 393. Why it matters. It is the source of the "need or benefit of the estate" test and of the alienee's duty to inquire. Vineeta Sharma v. Rakesh Sharma (2020) Facts. A three-judge bench answered a reference on how the substituted Section 6 applies to daughters. Principle. Without partition only an undivided share can be sold, not specific property, and whether consent is needed depends on the school (para 81). Once a share is determined it can be sold or mortgaged as separate property (para 80). Section 6(4) makes a daughter liable in the same manner as a son (para 61). Why it matters. It states the limits on a coparcener's alienation and on debt liability after 2005.

selfTest.q: 1. What does "antecedent" mean in antecedent debt?
selfTest.a: Antecedent in fact as well as in time: truly independent and not part of the transaction challenged ( Brij Narain , para 17(4)).

selfTest.q: 2. What is the test for the father's power to expose the estate to execution?
selfTest.a: The debt must not be for an immoral purpose ( Brij Narain , para 17(2)).

selfTest.q: 3. When does a mortgage by a father bind his sons' interest?
selfTest.a: When it is to discharge an antecedent debt of his that was not for an immoral or illegal purpose ( Brij Narain , para 17(3); Mulla, section 256). For debts after 9 September 2005, see Section 6(4).

selfTest.q: 4. When does a sale by a Karta who is not the father bind the family?
selfTest.a: When it is for legal necessity or for the benefit of the estate (Mulla, sections 242, 243, 243A).

selfTest.q: 5. Who must prove legal necessity?
selfTest.a: The buyer or mortgagee, who must prove necessity in fact or proper and honest inquiry (Mulla, section 244).

selfTest.q: 6. A lent ₹1,000 and interest has run to ₹1,200. Where damdupat applies, how much interest can A recover in a suit?
selfTest.a: The amount of the principal, ₹1,000 (Mulla, section 596).

సెక్షన్ 6(4). 9 సెప్టెంబర్ 2005 తర్వాత చేసిన అప్పు కోసం కేవలం పవిత్ర బాధ్యత కారణంగా రుణదాత కొడుకు, మనవడు, మునిమనవడిపై చర్య తీసుకోలేడు. అంతకు ముందటి అప్పుకు, ఆ తేదీకి ముందు పుట్టిన లేదా దత్తత తీసుకున్న వంశస్థులపై రుణదాత పాత హక్కు, ఆ అప్పు కోసం చేసిన అన్యాక్రాంతం కాపాడబడతాయి. సెక్షన్ 6(4) కూతురిని కొడుకు లాగే బాధ్యురాలిని చేస్తుందని Vineeta Sharma (para 61) జోడిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 6(1) నిబంధన. 20 డిసెంబర్ 2004 కు ముందు జరిగిన అమ్మకం, బహుమతి, తాకట్టు, విభజన లేదా వీలునామా ను కూతురి కొత్త హక్కు తిరగదోడదు. సెక్షన్ 30 Explanation. కోపార్సినర్ తన అవిభక్త హక్కును వీలునామా ద్వారా ఇవ్వవచ్చు. ఈ అంశంలో మిగిలినదంతా Brij Narain లో ప్రివీ కౌన్సిల్, ముల్లా చెప్పిన న్యాయమూర్తులు రూపొందించిన మితాక్షర చట్టం.

selfTest.q: 1. పూర్వపు అప్పులో "antecedent" అంటే ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: సమయంలోనూ, వాస్తవంలోనూ ముందుది: నిజంగా స్వతంత్రమైనది, సవాలు చేసిన లావాదేవీలో భాగం కానిది ( Brij Narain , para 17(4)).

selfTest.q: 2. ఎస్టేట్‌ను డిక్రీ అమలుకు గురిచేసే తండ్రి అధికారానికి పరీక్ష ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: అప్పు అనైతిక ప్రయోజనం కోసం కాకూడదు ( Brij Narain , para 17(2)).

selfTest.q: 3. తండ్రి తాకట్టు కొడుకుల హక్కును ఎప్పుడు బంధిస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: అనైతిక లేదా చట్టవిరుద్ధ ప్రయోజనం కోసం కాని అతని పూర్వపు అప్పు తీర్చడానికైతే ( Brij Narain , para 17(3); ముల్లా, సెక్షన్ 256). 9 సెప్టెంబర్ 2005 తర్వాతి అప్పులకు సెక్షన్ 6(4) చూడండి.

selfTest.q: 4. తండ్రి కాని కర్త చేసిన అమ్మకం కుటుంబాన్ని ఎప్పుడు బంధిస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: చట్టబద్ధమైన అవసరం లేదా ఎస్టేట్ ప్రయోజనం కోసమైతే (ముల్లా, సెక్షన్లు 242, 243, 243A).

selfTest.q: 5. చట్టబద్ధమైన అవసరాన్ని ఎవరు రుజువు చేయాలి?
selfTest.a: కొనేవారు లేదా తాకట్టుదారు; వాస్తవ అవసరాన్ని గానీ, సరైన నిజాయితీ విచారణను గానీ రుజువు చేయాలి (ముల్లా, సెక్షన్ 244).

selfTest.q: 6. A ₹1,000 అప్పు ఇచ్చాడు; వడ్డీ ₹1,200 కు చేరింది. దామ్‌దుపట్ వర్తించే చోట, దావాలో A ఎంత వడ్డీ వసూలు చేయగలడు?
selfTest.a: అసలు మొత్తం అయిన ₹1,000 (ముల్లా, సెక్షన్ 596).

family-law-i-u2-t1.subtitle: Meaning of Hindu marriage: a sacrament with contract-like features, and the Gandharva form

en.inOneMinute: No Act defines Hindu marriage in one sentence. The definition has to be built from the classical law and from the sections of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Classical law. Marriage was a sacrament , "a holy union for the performance of religious duties" (Mulla). In Tikait Mon Mohini Jemadai v. Basanta Kumar Singh (1901) the Calcutta High Court said that "though marriage under the Hindu Law is a contract, it is also a sacrament"; it is "more religious than secular in character" and "the union is indissoluble ". Under the 1955 Act. Mulla's commentary defines a Hindu marriage as "a union of one man with one woman to the exclusion of all others" made by the customary rites and ceremonies of either party. Once made, it creates "a relation and a status not imposed or defined by contract but by law". It is a sacred, ceremonial and monogamous union, which the law can now declare void, annul or dissolve. What exams ask. The sacrament and contract debate; Tikait ; the ceremonies required by Section 7 ( Bhaurao , Dolly Rani ); the contract-like features added in 1955; the eight classical forms; and the civil marriage under the Special Marriage Act, 1954.
legalProvision: The Act has no definition clause for "marriage". These sections together show what a Hindu marriage is in law.

Section 5, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Conditions for a Hindu marriage. A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus, if the following conditions are fulfilled, namely:— (i) neither party has a spouse living at the time of the marriage; (ii) at the time of the marriage, neither party— (a) is incapable of giving a valid consent to it in consequence of unsoundness of mind; or (b) though capable of giving a valid consent, has been suffering from mental disorder of such a kind or to such an extent as to be unfit for marriage and the procreation of children; or (c) has been subject to recurrent attacks of insanity; (iii) the bridegroom has completed the age of twenty-one years and the bride, the age of eighteen years at the time of the marriage; (iv) the parties are not within the degrees of prohibited relationship unless the custom or usage governing each of them permits of a marriage between the two; (v) the parties are not sapindas of each other, unless the custom or usage governing each of them permits of a marriage between the two;

Section 7. Ceremonies for a Hindu marriage. (1) A Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party thereto. (2) Where such rites and ceremonies include the Saptapadi (that is, the taking of seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire), the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.

Section 4. Overriding effect of Act. Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act,— (a) any text rule or interpretation of Hindu law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act; (b) any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act.
Section 8(5). Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, the validity of any Hindu marriage shall in no way be affected by the omission to make the entry.

Section 29(4). Nothing contained in this Act shall be deemed to affect the provisions contained in the Special Marriage Act, 1954 (43 of 1954) with respect to marriages between Hindus solemnized under that Act, whether before or after the commencement of this Act.

Section 12(2) proviso, Special Marriage Act, 1954. Provided that it shall not be complete and binding on the parties unless each party says to the other in the presence of the Marriage Officer and the three witnesses and in any language understood by the parties,—"I, (A), take thee (B), to be my lawful wife (or husband)".
In simple words

Section 5: a Hindu marriage can be made only between two Hindus who meet the conditions: no living spouse, sound mind, the minimum ages (21 and 18), and no prohibited relationship or sapinda relationship unless a custom governing each of them allows it. (Clause (vi), on the consent of the bride's guardian, was omitted in 1978.) Section 7: the marriage is made by the customary rites and ceremonies of either the bride's side or the bridegroom's side. If those rites include the saptapadi , the marriage is complete and binding when the seventh step is taken. Section 4: on every matter the Act deals with, the old texts, rules and customs of Hindu law stop applying. Other older laws stop applying only where they are inconsistent with the Act. Section 8(5): a Hindu marriage is not invalid only because it was not registered. Section 29(4): two Hindus may still marry under the Special Marriage Act, 1954, and that Act then governs their marriage. Special Marriage Act, Section 12(2): a civil marriage is complete only when each party makes the stated declaration to the other before the Marriage Officer and three witnesses.
en.meaning:
The question this topic answers. What is a Hindu marriage in law: a religious sacrament, a contract , or something else? Classical meaning. Mulla states the law before 1955 in these words: "Marriage, according to the Hindu law, is a holy union for the performance of religious duties. It is not a contract" (Mulla, section 427). The Introductory Note to the Hindu Marriage Act in Mulla adds: "In Hindu law marriage is treated as a samskara or a sacrament. It is the last of ten sacraments, enjoined by the Hindu religion for regeneration of men and obligatory in case of every Hindu who does not desire to adopt the life of a Sanyasi." Meaning under the Act (Mulla's definition). Mulla's commentary on Section 5 says: "A Hindu marriage under the Act, it is submitted, is not entirely or necessarily a sacrament (sanskara) but a union of one man with one woman to the exclusion of all others satisfied by solemnization of the customary rites and ceremonies of either party essential for a marriage: and directly it exists, creates a relation and a status not imposed or defined by contract but by law." The same passage says: "It is also not possible to say that the legal concept of marriage under the Act is one of contract." The four parts of this definition. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Mulla's definition, read with Sections 5 and 7: a ceremonial, monogamous union that creates a status fixed by law. flowchart TD M["Hindu marriage under the Act
(no statutory definition)"] M --> A["1. Union of one man
with one woman"] M --> B["2. To the exclusion of all others
no living spouse: s. 5(i)"] M --> C["3. Made by customary rites
of either party: s. 7"] M --> D["4. Creates a status
fixed by law, not by contract"] Text description A Hindu marriage under the Act has four parts: a union of one man with one woman; to the exclusion of all others, because neither party may have a living spouse under Section 5(i); made by the customary rites and ceremonies of either party under Section 7; and creating a status fixed by law, not by contract. A union of one man with one woman. It is between a bridegroom and a bride (Sections 5(iii) and 7(2) use these words). To the exclusion of all others. It is monogamous: neither party may have a living spouse (Section 5(i)). Made by ceremonies. It must be solemnized by the customary rites and ceremonies of either party (Section 7). Without them there is no Hindu marriage. It creates a status fixed by law. The rights and duties of husband and wife come from law, not from any agreement between them. Why the law has this rule. Marriage decides the status of the spouses, the legitimacy of children, maintenance and succession. The law therefore fixes how a marriage is made and what it means, and does not leave this to private agreement.
keyPoints: The Hindu Marriage Act has no definition of marriage; its meaning comes from Sections 5 and 7. Classical law: "a holy union for the performance of religious duties. It is not a contract" (Mulla, s. 427). Tikait (1901): "though ... a contract, it is also a sacrament"; "the union is indissoluble"; a pre-marriage deed varying marital rights is against public policy. Mulla's definition under the Act: a union of one man with one woman to the exclusion of all others, by the customary rites of either party, creating a status fixed by law, not by contract. Bhaurao (1965): without proper ceremonies there is no "solemnized" marriage, even in the Gandharva form. Dolly Rani (2024): no ceremony, no marriage; registration is only proof. The Act added consent, nullity, divorce, restitution, judicial separation and remarriage. Eight classical forms; only Brahma and Asura recognised before 1955; the Act names no form. Special Marriage Act, 1954: civil marriage between any two persons, by declaration before the Marriage Officer and three witnesses.

caseLaws.name: Tikait Mon Mohini Jemadai v
caseLaws.facts: Basanta Kumar Singh (1901) Facts. The parties married in 1885 as minors. At the marriage, a deed said the husband would never take his wife from her father's house and would obey her mother. After about fifteen years there, disputes arose, and he sued to make her live with him in his own house. Principle. Marriage "though ... a contract ... is also a sacrament" and "the union is indissoluble" (para 16). The rights and duties of marriage are fixed by law and cannot be varied by agreement (Banerjee, quoted at para 32); the deed was "opposed to public policy" (para 40). Appeal dismissed with costs. (1901) ILR 28 Cal 751. Why it matters. It is the classic authority for the sacramental view, and for the rule that the incidents of marriage are fixed by law. Bhaurao Shankar Lokhande v. State of Maharashtra (1965) Facts. Bhaurao, married to Indubai in about 1956, married Kamlabai in 1962 while Indubai was alive, and was convicted of bigamy. The State said the second marriage was a Gandharva marriage as modified by custom; the invocation before fire and the saptapadi were not performed. Principle. "Solemnize" means to celebrate with proper ceremonies and in due form; the two essential ceremonies are part of a Gandharva marriage too unless custom has modified them. The second marriage was not "solemnized", so the convictions were set aside. AIR 1965 SC 1564 : (1965) 2 SCR 837. Why it matters. It shows that consent without the essential ceremonies does not make a Hindu marriage. Dolly Rani v. Manish Kumar Chanchal (2024) Facts. Two pilots obtained a society's marriage certificate in 2021 and registered the marriage under the Uttar Pradesh rules, planning the ceremony for 2022. No rites were performed. Disputes and cases followed, and both told the Court that no marriage had been solemnized. Principle. Without the Section 7 ceremonies there is no Hindu marriage; a certificate or registration "would neither confirm any marital status ... nor establish a marriage". A Hindu marriage "is a samskara and a sacrament"; "A marriage is not a commercial transaction." The Court declared there was no marriage and quashed the cases. 2024 INSC 355. Why it matters. It restates, for today, that a Hindu marriage is a ceremonial and sacred union, and that registration is only proof.

selfTest.q: 1. Does the Hindu Marriage Act define "marriage"?
selfTest.a: No. Its meaning is gathered from Sections 5 and 7, the case law and Mulla.

selfTest.q: 2. What did the Calcutta High Court say about Hindu marriage in Tikait?
selfTest.a: "Though marriage under the Hindu Law is a contract, it is also a sacrament"; it is more religious than secular, and the union is indissoluble (para 16).

selfTest.q: 4. Is a Gandharva marriage made by consent alone?
selfTest.a: No. The essential ceremonies are needed in this form too, unless custom has modified them (Mulla; Bhaurao ).

selfTest.q: 5. A couple registers their marriage but performs no ceremony. Are they married under the Act?
selfTest.a: No. Without Section 7 ceremonies there is no Hindu marriage, and registration cannot create one ( Dolly Rani ; Section 8(5) only protects a marriage that was solemnized but not registered).

selfTest.q: 6. Which two classical forms were recognised before 1955, and what was the difference?
selfTest.a: The Brahma form, a gift of the bride without consideration, and the Asura form, where the guardian received shulka (bride's price).

Section 5, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Conditions for a Hindu marriage. A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus, if the following conditions are fulfilled, namely:— (i) neither party has a spouse living at the time of the marriage; (ii) at the time of the marriage, neither party— (a) is incapable of giving a valid consent to it in consequence of unsoundness of mind; or (b) though capable of giving a valid consent, has been suffering from mental disorder of such a kind or to such an extent as to be unfit for marriage and the procreation of children; or (c) has been subject to recurrent attacks of insanity; (iii) the bridegroom has completed the age of twenty-one years and the bride, the age of eighteen years at the time of the marriage; (iv) the parties are not within the degrees of prohibited relationship unless the custom or usage governing each of them permits of a marriage between the two; (v) the parties are not sapindas of each other, unless the custom or usage governing each of them permits of a marriage between the two;

Section 7. Ceremonies for a Hindu marriage. (1) A Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party thereto. (2) Where such rites and ceremonies include the Saptapadi (that is, the taking of seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire), the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.

Section 4. Overriding effect of Act. Save as otherwise expressly provided in this Act,— (a) any text rule or interpretation of Hindu law or any custom or usage as part of that law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect with respect to any matter for which provision is made in this Act; (b) any other law in force immediately before the commencement of this Act shall cease to have effect in so far as it is inconsistent with any of the provisions contained in this Act.
Section 8(5). Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, the validity of any Hindu marriage shall in no way be affected by the omission to make the entry.

Section 29(4). Nothing contained in this Act shall be deemed to affect the provisions contained in the Special Marriage Act, 1954 (43 of 1954) with respect to marriages between Hindus solemnized under that Act, whether before or after the commencement of this Act.

Section 12(2) proviso, Special Marriage Act, 1954. Provided that it shall not be complete and binding on the parties unless each party says to the other in the presence of the Marriage Officer and the three witnesses and in any language understood by the parties,—"I, (A), take thee (B), to be my lawful wife (or husband)".

సెక్షన్ 5: షరతులు నెరవేర్చిన ఇద్దరు హిందువుల మధ్యే హిందూ వివాహం జరగగలదు: జీవించి ఉన్న జీవిత భాగస్వామి ఉండకూడదు, మానసిక స్థిరత్వం ఉండాలి, కనీస వయస్సులు (21, 18) ఉండాలి, ఇద్దరినీ పాలించే ఆచారం అనుమతిస్తే తప్ప నిషిద్ధ సంబంధం లేదా సపిండ సంబంధం ఉండకూడదు. (వధువు సంరక్షకుని సమ్మతి గురించిన క్లాజు (vi) 1978 లో తొలగించబడింది.) సెక్షన్ 7: వధువు పక్షం లేదా వరుడి పక్షం, ఏదో ఒకరి ఆచార కర్మలు, వేడుకలతో వివాహం జరుగుతుంది. ఆ కర్మల్లో సప్తపది ఉంటే, ఏడో అడుగు వేసినప్పుడు వివాహం పూర్తై, కట్టుబడి ఉంటుంది. సెక్షన్ 4: చట్టం వ్యవహరించే ప్రతి విషయంలో, హిందూ చట్టపు పాత గ్రంథాలు, నియమాలు, ఆచారాలు వర్తించడం ఆగిపోతుంది. ఇతర పాత చట్టాలు చట్టానికి విరుద్ధంగా ఉన్నంత వరకే వర్తించడం ఆగిపోతాయి. సెక్షన్ 8(5): రిజిస్టర్ చేయలేదనే కారణం మాత్రాన హిందూ వివాహం చెల్లకుండా పోదు. సెక్షన్ 29(4): ఇద్దరు హిందువులు ఇప్పటికీ ప్రత్యేక వివాహ చట్టం, 1954 కింద పెళ్లి చేసుకోవచ్చు; అప్పుడు ఆ చట్టమే వారి వివాహాన్ని పాలిస్తుంది. ప్రత్యేక వివాహ చట్టం, సెక్షన్ 12(2): మ్యారేజ్ ఆఫీసర్, ముగ్గురు సాక్షుల సమక్షంలో ప్రతి పక్షం మరొకరికి పేర్కొన్న ప్రకటన చేసినప్పుడే పౌర వివాహం పూర్తవుతుంది.

ఈ అంశం జవాబిచ్చే ప్రశ్న. చట్టంలో హిందూ వివాహం అంటే ఏమిటి: మతపరమైన సంస్కారమా, ఒప్పందమా, లేక మరేదైనానా? సంప్రదాయ అర్థం. 1955 కి ముందు చట్టాన్ని ముల్లా ఈ మాటల్లో చెబుతారు: "Marriage, according to the Hindu law, is a holy union for the performance of religious duties. It is not a contract " (ముల్లా, సెక్షన్ 427). ముల్లాలోని హిందూ వివాహ చట్టపు Introductory Note ఇలా జోడిస్తుంది: "In Hindu law marriage is treated as a samskara or a sacrament. It is the last of ten sacraments, enjoined by the Hindu religion for regeneration of men and obligatory in case of every Hindu who does not desire to adopt the life of a Sanyasi." చట్టం కింద అర్థం (ముల్లా నిర్వచనం). సెక్షన్ 5 పై ముల్లా వ్యాఖ్యానం ఇలా చెబుతుంది: "A Hindu marriage under the Act, it is submitted, is not entirely or necessarily a sacrament (sanskara) but a union of one man with one woman to the exclusion of all others satisfied by solemnization of the customary rites and ceremonies of either party essential for a marriage: and directly it exists, creates a relation and a status not imposed or defined by contract but by law." అదే భాగం ఇలా కూడా చెబుతుంది: "It is also not possible to say that the legal concept of marriage under the Act is one of contract." ఈ నిర్వచనంలోని నాలుగు భాగాలు. ఆచార కర్మలతో: సె. 7"] M --> D["4. ఒప్పందం కాదు, చట్టం
నిర్ణయించే హోదా ఏర్పడుతుంది"] వచన వివరణ చట్టం ప్రకారం హిందూ వివాహానికి నాలుగు భాగాలు: ఒక పురుషుడు, ఒక స్త్రీ కలయిక; సెక్షన్ 5(i) ప్రకారం ఎవరికీ జీవించి ఉన్న జీవిత భాగస్వామి ఉండకూడదు కాబట్టి ఇతరులందరినీ మినహాయించి; సెక్షన్ 7 ప్రకారం ఏదో ఒక పక్షం ఆచార కర్మలు, వేడుకలతో జరిగేది; ఒప్పందం కాకుండా చట్టం నిర్ణయించే హోదాను సృష్టించేది. ఒక పురుషుడు, ఒక స్త్రీ కలయిక. ఇది వరుడు, వధువు మధ్య జరిగేది (సెక్షన్లు 5(iii), 7(2) ఈ పదాలు వాడతాయి). ఇతరులందరినీ మినహాయించి. ఇది ఏకపత్నీ వివాహం: ఏ పక్షానికీ జీవించి ఉన్న జీవిత భాగస్వామి ఉండకూడదు (సెక్షన్ 5(i)). వేడుకలతో జరిగేది. ఏదో ఒక పక్షం ఆచార కర్మలు, వేడుకలతో దీనిని నిర్వహించాలి (సెక్షన్ 7). అవి లేకుండా హిందూ వివాహం లేదు. చట్టం నిర్ణయించే హోదాను సృష్టిస్తుంది. భార్యాభర్తల హక్కులు, బాధ్యతలు వారి మధ్య ఒప్పందం నుంచి కాదు, చట్టం నుంచి వస్తాయి. చట్టం ఈ నియమం ఎందుకు పెట్టింది. వివాహం భార్యాభర్తల హోదాను, పిల్లల చట్టబద్ధతను, భరణాన్ని, వారసత్వాన్ని నిర్ణయిస్తుంది. అందుకే వివాహం ఎలా జరుగుతుందో, దాని అర్థం ఏమిటో చట్టమే నిర్ణయిస్తుంది; దానిని వ్యక్తిగత ఒప్పందానికి వదలదు.

selfTest.q: 1. హిందూ వివాహ చట్టం "వివాహం" ను నిర్వచిస్తుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. దాని అర్థాన్ని సెక్షన్లు 5, 7, కేసు చట్టం, ముల్లా నుంచి కూర్చుకోవాలి.

selfTest.q: 2. Tikait లో కలకత్తా హైకోర్టు హిందూ వివాహం గురించి ఏమి చెప్పింది?
selfTest.a: "Though marriage under the Hindu Law is a contract, it is also a sacrament"; అది లౌకికం కంటే ఎక్కువ మతపరమైనది, ఆ కలయిక విడదీయరానిది (పేరా 16).

selfTest.q: 4. గాంధర్వ వివాహం సమ్మతి మాత్రంతో జరుగుతుందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. ఆచారం మార్చకపోతే ఈ రూపంలో కూడా ముఖ్యమైన వేడుకలు అవసరం (ముల్లా; Bhaurao ).

selfTest.q: 5. ఒక జంట వివాహాన్ని రిజిస్టర్ చేసింది, కానీ ఏ వేడుకా జరపలేదు. వారు చట్టం కింద వివాహితులా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. సెక్షన్ 7 వేడుకలు లేకుండా హిందూ వివాహం లేదు, రిజిస్ట్రేషన్ దానిని సృష్టించలేదు ( Dolly Rani ; సెక్షన్ 8(5) జరిగి రిజిస్టర్ కాని వివాహాన్ని మాత్రమే కాపాడుతుంది).

selfTest.q: 6. 1955 కి ముందు గుర్తించిన రెండు సంప్రదాయ రూపాలు ఏవి, వాటి తేడా ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: బ్రహ్మ రూపం, ప్రతిఫలం లేకుండా వధువు దానం; అసుర రూపం, సంరక్షకుడు శుల్కం (వధువు ధర) తీసుకునేది.

family-law-i-u2-t2.subtitle: Why the law protects marriage: religious, social and legal importance, and the presumption in its favour

en.inOneMinute: Marriage is the base of the Hindu family, and its importance is of three kinds. Religious. Hindu law treats marriage as a samskara , a sacrament. In Tikait (1901) the Calcutta High Court called it "more religious than secular in character". Social. In Sarla Mudgal (1995) the Supreme Court said: "Marriage is an institution in the maintenance of which the public at large is deeply interested. It is the foundation of the family and in turn of the society without which no civilisation can exist." Legal. Many rights flow from the status of husband and wife: maintenance, legitimacy of children, succession, a right to reside, and the matrimonial remedies. Because so much depends on it, the law protects marriage. It keeps children legitimate even when a marriage is void or annulled (Section 16). It also presumes a valid marriage where a man and a woman have lived together for a long time as husband and wife ( Badri Prasad , 1978). The presumption can be rebutted.
legalProvision: Section 16, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Legitimacy of children of void and voidable marriages. (1) Notwithstanding that a marriage is null and void under section 11, any child of such marriage who would have been legitimate if the marriage had been valid, shall be legitimate, whether such child is born before or after the commencement of the Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976 (68 of 1976), and whether or not a decree of nullity is granted in respect of that marriage under this Act and whether or not the marriage is held to be void otherwise than on a petition under this Act. (2) Where a decree of nullity is granted in respect of a voidable marriage under section 12, any child begotten or conceived before the decree is made, who would have been the legitimate child of the parties to the marriage if at the date of the decree it had been dissolved instead of being annulled, shall be deemed to be their legitimate child notwithstanding the decree of nullity. (3) Nothing contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) shall be construed as conferring upon any child of a marriage which is null and void or which is annulled by a decree of nullity under section 12, any rights in or to the property of any person, other than the parents, in any case where, but for the passing of this Act, such child would have been incapable of possessing or acquiring any such rights by reason of his not being the legitimate child of his parents.

Section 24. Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings. Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application of the wife or the husband, order the respondent to pay to the petitioner the expenses of the proceeding, and monthly during the proceeding such sum as, having regard to the petitioner's own income and the income of the respondent, it may seem to the court to be reasonable.

Section 25(1). Permanent alimony and maintenance. Any court exercising jurisdiction under this Act may, at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent thereto, on application made to it for the purpose by either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, order that the respondent shall pay to the applicant for her or his maintenance and support such gross sum or such monthly or periodical sum for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant as, having regard to the respondent's own income and other property, if any, the income and other property of the applicant, the conduct of the parties and other circumstances of the case, it may seem to the court to be just, and any such payment may be secured, if necessary, by a charge on the immovable property of the respondent.
Section 8(5). Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, the validity of any Hindu marriage shall in no way be affected by the omission to make the entry.

Section 18(1), Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. Subject to the provisions of this section, a Hindu wife, whether married before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her life time.
In simple words

Section 16(1): a child of a void marriage is legitimate, as if the marriage had been valid. No decree of nullity is needed for this. Section 16(2): when a voidable marriage is annulled, a child begotten or conceived before the decree is legitimate. Section 16(3): such a child gets rights in the property of the parents only, not of other relatives, where the child would otherwise have had no such right. Section 24: during a case under the Act, a spouse (wife or husband) without enough income may get the expenses of the case and a monthly sum. The proviso adds that the application should, as far as possible, be decided within sixty days from service of notice. Section 25(1): when or after the court passes a decree, either spouse may get maintenance for life at most, as a gross sum or a periodical sum, which may be secured by a charge on the other's immovable property. Section 8(5): not registering a marriage does not make it invalid. HAMA Section 18(1): a Hindu wife is entitled to be maintained by her husband for her whole life.
en.meaning:
Meaning. The importance of the institution of marriage is the set of religious, social and legal functions it performs for the spouses, their children and society. Mulla's Introductory Note to the Hindu Marriage Act says: "Marriage is necessarily the basis of social organisation and the foundation of important legal rights and obligations." The question this topic answers. Why does Hindu law treat marriage as an institution to be protected, and how does it protect it? The two halves of the answer. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. Three kinds of importance, and four ways the law protects marriage. flowchart TD M["Institution of marriage"] M --> W["Why it matters"] M --> P["How the law protects it"] W --> R["Religious: samskara
(Tikait, Mulla)"] W --> S["Social: public deeply interested
(Sarla Mudgal)"] W --> L["Legal: rights flow from
the status of spouse"] P --> P1["Rights: maintenance, succession,
residence, remedies"] P --> P2["Children legitimate
even if marriage fails: s. 16"] P --> P3["Presumption from
long cohabitation (Badri Prasad)"] P --> P4["Registration as proof:
s. 8 (Seema)"] Text description Marriage has religious importance (a samskara), social importance (the public is deeply interested in it) and legal importance (rights flow from the status of spouse). The law protects it by attaching rights of maintenance, succession and residence and the matrimonial remedies; by keeping children legitimate under Section 16; by presuming a marriage from long cohabitation; and by registration as proof. Why marriage matters: its religious, social and legal importance. How the law protects it: by the rights it attaches to marriage, by protecting children when a marriage fails, by the presumption in favour of marriage, and by providing for proof through registration. Why the law has this rule. Marriage is a status that others rely on: the spouses, their children, their families and the public. Mulla, explaining the meaning of status, quotes: the relation of the parties and their status "are not imposed or defined by contract or agreement but by law". If marriage could be easily denied, the wife's maintenance and the children's legitimacy and inheritance would be put at risk.
keyPoints: Marriage has religious, social and legal importance. Tikait : "more religious than secular in character"; Mulla: the last of ten sacraments. Sarla Mudgal : "the public at large is deeply interested" in maintaining marriage. Maintenance (HMA ss. 24–25 for either spouse; HAMA s. 18 for the wife; BNSS s. 144) and succession (HSA ss. 8, 15) depend on the status of spouse. Section 16 keeps children of void and voidable marriages legitimate; their property rights are limited to the parents' property. Long open cohabitation raises a strong but rebuttable presumption of marriage; a heavy burden lies on the person who denies it ( Badri Prasad ). Registration helps to prove a marriage but does not decide validity (s. 8(5); Seema ).

caseLaws.name: Badri Prasad v
caseLaws.facts: Deputy Director of Consolidation (1978) Facts. A man and a woman lived together as husband and wife for about fifty years. The petitioner challenged the fact of their marriage, in proceedings to which the Deputy Director of Consolidation was a party, arguing that no priest or other witness of the ceremony had been examined. The Allahabad High Court rejected the challenge. Principle. A strong presumption of wedlock arises from a long spell of living together as husband and wife; it is rebuttable, but a heavy burden lies on the person who denies it; "Law leans in favour of legitimacy and frowns upon bastardy." Special leave petitions dismissed. AIR 1978 SC 1557 : (1978) 3 SCC 527. Why it matters. It is the leading statement of the presumption in favour of marriage. Sarla Mudgal v. Union of India (1995) Facts. Hindu husbands with living Hindu wives converted to Islam and married again. One wife, Meena Mathur, learnt that her husband had married a second time after both he and the second woman converted. Principle. "Marriage is an institution in the maintenance of which the public at large is deeply interested"; the second marriage of a Hindu husband after conversion, without dissolving the first, is void and he is guilty under Section 494 IPC. (1995) 3 SCC 635 : AIR 1995 SC 1531. Why it matters. It is the leading statement of the social importance of marriage. Seema v. Ashwani Kumar (2006) Facts. While hearing a transfer petition, the Supreme Court noted that persons were denying the existence of marriages because most States kept no official record. It heard the States and the National Commission for Women on registration. Principle. Registration is not proof of a valid marriage "per se" and does not decide validity, but "it has a great evidentiary value"; marriages of all citizens should be made compulsorily registrable, and the States were directed to notify rules. Decided 14 February 2006. Why it matters. It explains the place of registration in protecting marriage, especially for women.

selfTest.q: 1. Which section protects the legitimacy of children of void marriages?
selfTest.a: Section 16(1) of the Hindu Marriage Act.

selfTest.q: 2. What does long, open cohabitation as husband and wife raise?
selfTest.a: A strong presumption of marriage, which is rebuttable; a heavy burden lies on the person who denies it ( Badri Prasad ).

selfTest.q: 3. Does non-registration affect validity?
selfTest.a: No. Section 8(5).

selfTest.q: 4. Can a husband claim maintenance under the Hindu Marriage Act?
selfTest.a: Yes. Sections 24 and 25 allow "either the wife or the husband" to apply.

selfTest.q: 5. Does "wife" in BNSS Section 144 include a divorced woman?
selfTest.a: Yes, if she has not remarried (Explanation to Section 144(1)).

selfTest.q: 6. Is the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856 still in force?
selfTest.a: No. It was repealed in 1983. A widow's remarriage is now governed by the Hindu Marriage Act.

legalProvision: Section 16, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Legitimacy of children of void and voidable marriages. (1) Notwithstanding that a marriage is null and void under section 11, any child of such marriage who would have been legitimate if the marriage had been valid, shall be legitimate, whether such child is born before or after the commencement of the Marriage Laws (Amendment) Act, 1976 (68 of 1976), and whether or not a decree of nullity is granted in respect of that marriage under this Act and whether or not the marriage is held to be void otherwise than on a petition under this Act. (2) Where a decree of nullity is granted in respect of a voidable marriage under section 12, any child begotten or conceived before the decree is made, who would have been the legitimate child of the parties to the marriage if at the date of the decree it had been dissolved instead of being annulled, shall be deemed to be their legitimate child notwithstanding the decree of nullity. (3) Nothing contained in sub-section (1) or sub-section (2) shall be construed as conferring upon any child of a marriage which is null and void or which is annulled by a decree of nullity under section 12, any rights in or to the property of any person, other than the parents, in any case where, but for the passing of this Act, such child would have been incapable of possessing or acquiring any such rights by reason of his not being the legitimate child of his parents.

Section 24. Maintenance pendente lite and expenses of proceedings. Where in any proceeding under this Act it appears to the court that either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, has no independent income sufficient for her or his support and the necessary expenses of the proceeding, it may, on the application of the wife or the husband, order the respondent to pay to the petitioner the expenses of the proceeding, and monthly during the proceeding such sum as, having regard to the petitioner's own income and the income of the respondent, it may seem to the court to be reasonable.

Section 25(1). Permanent alimony and maintenance. Any court exercising jurisdiction under this Act may, at the time of passing any decree or at any time subsequent thereto, on application made to it for the purpose by either the wife or the husband, as the case may be, order that the respondent shall pay to the applicant for her or his maintenance and support such gross sum or such monthly or periodical sum for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant as, having regard to the respondent's own income and other property, if any, the income and other property of the applicant, the conduct of the parties and other circumstances of the case, it may seem to the court to be just, and any such payment may be secured, if necessary, by a charge on the immovable property of the respondent.
Section 8(5). Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, the validity of any Hindu marriage shall in no way be affected by the omission to make the entry.

Section 18(1), Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956. Subject to the provisions of this section, a Hindu wife, whether married before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be entitled to be maintained by her husband during her life time.

సెక్షన్ 16(1): శూన్య వివాహపు బిడ్డ, వివాహం చెల్లుబాటయ్యేదైతే ఎలాగో అలాగే చట్టబద్ధుడు. దీనికి శూన్యత డిక్రీ అవసరం లేదు. సెక్షన్ 16(2): రద్దు చేయదగిన వివాహం రద్దైనప్పుడు, డిక్రీకి ముందు పుట్టిన లేదా గర్భంలో ఉన్న బిడ్డ చట్టబద్ధుడు. సెక్షన్ 16(3): లేకపోతే హక్కు ఉండని చోట, అలాంటి బిడ్డకు తల్లిదండ్రుల ఆస్తిలోనే హక్కులు వస్తాయి, ఇతర బంధువుల ఆస్తిలో కాదు. సెక్షన్ 24: చట్టం కింద కేసు నడుస్తున్నప్పుడు, తగినంత ఆదాయం లేని జీవిత భాగస్వామి (భార్య లేదా భర్త) కేసు ఖర్చులు, నెలవారీ మొత్తం పొందవచ్చు. నోటీసు అందిన తేదీ నుంచి అరవై రోజుల్లో, సాధ్యమైనంత వరకు, దరఖాస్తును పరిష్కరించాలని ప్రొవిజో చెబుతుంది. సెక్షన్ 25(1): కోర్టు డిక్రీ ఇచ్చేటప్పుడు లేదా తర్వాత, ఏ జీవిత భాగస్వామైనా గరిష్ఠంగా జీవితకాలానికి, ఒకేసారి లేదా కాలానుగుణ మొత్తంగా భరణం పొందవచ్చు; దానిని మరొకరి స్థిరాస్తిపై చార్జీగా భద్రపరచవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 8(5): వివాహాన్ని రిజిస్టర్ చేయకపోవడం దానిని చెల్లకుండా చేయదు. HAMA సెక్షన్ 18(1): హిందూ భార్య తన జీవితాంతం భర్త నుంచి భరణం పొందే హక్కు కలిగి ఉంటుంది.

అర్థం. వివాహ వ్యవస్థ ప్రాముఖ్యత అంటే, అది భార్యాభర్తలకు, వారి పిల్లలకు, సమాజానికి చేసే మతపరమైన, సామాజిక, చట్టపరమైన పనుల సమూహం. హిందూ వివాహ చట్టంపై ముల్లా Introductory Note ఇలా చెబుతుంది: "Marriage is necessarily the basis of social organisation and the foundation of important legal rights and obligations." ఈ అంశం జవాబిచ్చే ప్రశ్న. హిందూ చట్టం వివాహాన్ని కాపాడాల్సిన వ్యవస్థగా ఎందుకు భావిస్తుంది, దానిని ఎలా కాపాడుతుంది? జవాబులో రెండు భాగాలు. సె. 8 (Seema)"] వచన వివరణ వివాహానికి మతపరమైన ప్రాముఖ్యత (సంస్కారం), సామాజిక ప్రాముఖ్యత (ప్రజలకు దానిపై లోతైన ఆసక్తి), చట్టపరమైన ప్రాముఖ్యత (భార్యాభర్తల హోదా నుంచి హక్కులు వస్తాయి) ఉన్నాయి. భరణం, వారసత్వం, నివాస హక్కులు, వైవాహిక పరిష్కారాలు ఇవ్వడం ద్వారా; సెక్షన్ 16 కింద పిల్లల చట్టబద్ధతను కాపాడటం ద్వారా; దీర్ఘ సహజీవనం నుంచి వివాహాన్ని ఊహించడం ద్వారా; రుజువుగా రిజిస్ట్రేషన్ ద్వారా చట్టం దానిని కాపాడుతుంది. వివాహం ఎందుకు ముఖ్యం: దాని మతపరమైన, సామాజిక, చట్టపరమైన ప్రాముఖ్యత. చట్టం దానిని ఎలా కాపాడుతుంది: వివాహానికి హక్కులు జోడించడం ద్వారా, వివాహం విఫలమైనప్పుడు పిల్లలను కాపాడటం ద్వారా, వివాహానికి అనుకూలమైన ఊహ ద్వారా, రిజిస్ట్రేషన్ ద్వారా రుజువుకు అవకాశం ఇవ్వడం ద్వారా. చట్టం ఈ నియమం ఎందుకు పెట్టింది. వివాహం ఇతరులు ఆధారపడే హోదా: భార్యాభర్తలు, వారి పిల్లలు, కుటుంబాలు, ప్రజలు. హోదా అర్థాన్ని వివరిస్తూ ముల్లా ఇలా ఉటంకిస్తారు: పక్షాల సంబంధం, వారి హోదా "are not imposed or defined by contract or agreement but by law". వివాహాన్ని సులభంగా తిరస్కరించగలిగితే, భార్య భరణం, పిల్లల చట్టబద్ధత, వారసత్వం ప్రమాదంలో పడతాయి.

selfTest.q: 1. శూన్య వివాహాల పిల్లల చట్టబద్ధతను ఏ సెక్షన్ కాపాడుతుంది?
selfTest.a: హిందూ వివాహ చట్టం సెక్షన్ 16(1).

selfTest.q: 2. భార్యాభర్తలుగా దీర్ఘకాలం బహిరంగ సహజీవనం దేనిని కలిగిస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: వివాహానికి బలమైన ఊహను; అది ఖండించదగినది; తిరస్కరించే వ్యక్తిపై భారీ భారం ఉంటుంది ( Badri Prasad ).

selfTest.q: 3. రిజిస్టర్ చేయకపోవడం చెల్లుబాటును ప్రభావితం చేస్తుందా?
4. హిందూ వివాహ చట్టం కింద భర్త భరణం కోరగలడా?
selfTest.a: అవును. సెక్షన్లు 24, 25 "either the wife or the husband" దరఖాస్తు చేయడానికి అనుమతిస్తాయి.

selfTest.q: 5. BNSS సెక్షన్ 144 లో "wife" లో విడాకులు పొందిన స్త్రీ ఉంటుందా?
selfTest.a: అవును, ఆమె మళ్ళీ పెళ్లి చేసుకోకపోతే (సెక్షన్ 144(1) కి Explanation).

selfTest.q: 6. హిందూ విధవల పునర్వివాహ చట్టం, 1856 ఇంకా అమలులో ఉందా?
selfTest.a: లేదు. అది 1983 లో రద్దైంది. విధవ పునర్వివాహం ఇప్పుడు హిందూ వివాహ చట్టం కింద వస్తుంది.

family-law-i-u2-t3.subtitle: The five conditions of section 5 and what follows when each is broken

en.inOneMinute: Section 5 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (HMA) says a marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus if five conditions are met: No living spouse – neither party has a husband or wife living (clause (i)). Mental capacity – neither party is of unsound mind, mentally unfit for marriage and procreation, or subject to recurrent attacks of insanity (clause (ii)). Age – the bridegroom has completed 21 years and the bride 18 years (clause (iii)). No prohibited relationship – unless the custom of each party permits (clause (iv)). Not sapindas – unless the custom of each party permits (clause (v)). The results of a breach are not the same, and exams test this: Breach of clause (i), (iv) or (v): the marriage is void (Section 11). Breach of clause (i) is also the offence of bigamy (Section 17). Breach of clause (ii): the marriage is voidable (Section 12(1)(b)). Breach of clause (iii): the marriage stays valid under the HMA, but the person who procured it is punishable (Section 18(a)). The Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 (PCMA) separately lets the party who was a child have it annulled (PCMA Section 3). There was once a clause (vi) (consent of the bride's guardian). It was omitted in 1978. Same gotra, same pravara and different castes are no longer bars.
legalProvision: Section 5, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Conditions for a Hindu marriage. A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus, if the following conditions are fulfilled, namely:— (i) neither party has a spouse living at the time of the marriage; (ii) at the time of the marriage, neither party— (a) is incapable of giving a valid consent to it in consequence of unsoundness of mind; or (b) though capable of giving a valid consent, has been suffering from mental disorder of such a kind or to such an extent as to be unfit for marriage and the procreation of children; or (c) has been subject to recurrent attacks of insanity; (iii) the bridegroom has completed the age of twenty-one years and the bride, the age of eighteen years at the time of the marriage; (iv) the parties are not within the degrees of prohibited relationship unless the custom or usage governing each of them permits of a marriage between the two; (v) the parties are not sapindas of each other, unless the custom or usage governing each of them permits of a marriage between the two;

Notes from the bare Act: clause (ii) was substituted by Act 68 of 1976. The words "or epilepsy" were omitted from clause (ii)(c) by Act 39 of 1999 (from 29 December 1999). In clause (iii) the ages were "eighteen" and "fifteen" until Act 2 of 1978 raised them to twenty-one and eighteen (from 1 October 1978). Clause (vi) was omitted by the same Act of 1978.

Section 3(a). the expressions "custom" and "usage" signify any rule which, having been continuously and uniformly observed for a long time, has obtained the force of law among Hindus in any local area, tribe, community, group or family: Provided that the rule is certain and not unreasonable or opposed to public policy; and Provided further that in the case of a rule applicable only to a family it has not been discontinued by the family;

Section 3(f). (i) "sapinda relationship" with reference to any person extends as far as the third generation (inclusive) in the line of ascent through the mother, and the fifth (inclusive) in the line of ascent through the father, the line being traced upwards in each case from the person concerned, who is to be counted as the first generation; (ii) two persons are said to be "sapindas" of each other if one is a lineal ascendant of the other within the limits of sapinda relationship, or if they have a common lineal ascendant who is within the limits of sapinda relationship with reference to each of them;

Section 3(g). "degrees of prohibited relationship"—two persons are said to be within the "degrees of prohibited relationship"— (i) if one is a lineal ascendant of the other; or (ii) if one was the wife or husband of a lineal ascendant or descendant of the other; or (iii) if one was the wife of the brother or of the father's or mother's brother or of the grandfather's or grandmother's brother of the other; or (iv) if the two are brother and sister, uncle and niece, aunt and nephew, or children of brother and sister or of two brothers or of two sisters; Explanation. —For the purposes of clauses (f) and (g), relationship includes— (i) relationship by half or uterine blood as well as by full blood; (ii) illegitimate blood relationship as well as legitimate; (iii) relationship by adoption as well as by blood; and all terms of relationship in those clauses shall be construed accordingly.

Section 11. Void marriages. Any marriage solemnised after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void and may, on a petition presented by either party thereto against the other party, be so declared by a decree of nullity if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of section 5.

Section 12(1)(b). Voidable marriages. Any marriage solemnised, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be voidable and may be annulled by a decree of nullity on any of the following grounds, namely:— … (b) that the marriage is in contravention of the condition specified in clause (ii) of section 5;

Section 17. Punishment of bigamy. Any marriage between two Hindus solemnized after the commencement of this Act is void if at the date of such marriage either party had a husband or wife living; and the provisions of sections 494 and 495 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (45 of 1860), shall apply accordingly.

Section 18. Punishment for contravention of certain other conditions for a Hindu marriage. Every person who procures a marriage of himself or herself to be solemnized under this Act in contravention of the conditions specified in clauses (iii), (iv), and (v) of section 5 shall be punishable— (a) in the case of contravention of the condition specified in clause (iii) of section 5, with rigorous imprisonment which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both. (b) in the case of a contravention of the condition specified in clause (iv) or clause (v) of section 5, with simple imprisonment which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both;
Clause (a) of Section 18 was substituted by Section 20 of the PCMA (from 30 October 2007). A former clause (c), on the guardian's consent, was omitted in 1978.

In simple words: Section 5 lists what the two persons must satisfy on the wedding day. Sections 3(a), (f) and (g) explain the words used. Sections 11, 12, 17 and 18 say what happens if a condition is broken. The ceremonies themselves are a separate requirement (Section 7, covered in "Ceremonies and Registration").
en.meaning:
The conditions of a Hindu marriage are the legal requirements that the two parties must satisfy at the time of the marriage . A marriage that satisfies them, and is solemnized with the ceremonies required by Section 7, is a valid Hindu marriage. Three points come straight from the words of Section 5: "between any two Hindus". Both parties must be persons to whom the Act applies (Section 2). If one party is not a Hindu, a marriage under the HMA is not possible; the parties may marry under the Special Marriage Act, 1954. "at the time of the marriage". Each condition is tested on the date of the wedding. A spouse who dies a week after a second wedding does not make that wedding valid. Not every condition has the same weight. Breach of some conditions destroys the marriage (void), breach of one makes it open to challenge (voidable), and breach of the age condition only attracts punishment. See Diagram 1 for the step-by-step test. Diagram 1. Test the five conditions in this order; the first "Yes" gives the result. flowchart TD Q1{"Either party had a

no custom of each permitting?
s. 5(iv), (v)"} Q3 -->|"Yes"| V3["VOID: s. 11

bride under 18? s. 5(iii)"} Q4 -->|"Yes"| V4["VALID but punishable: s. 18(a)
voidable at child's option:
PCMA s. 3"] Q4 -->|"No"| V5["VALID, if s. 7
ceremonies performed"] Text description First ask whether either party had a living spouse; if yes, the marriage is void and bigamy is punishable under sections 11 and 17. If no, ask whether either party lacked mental capacity; if yes, it is voidable under section 12(1)(b). If no, ask whether the parties are within prohibited degrees or are sapindas with no custom of each permitting it; if yes, it is void under section 11 and punishable under section 18(b). If no, ask whether the groom is under 21 or the bride under 18; if yes, it is valid but punishable under section 18(a), and voidable at the child's option under PCMA section 3. If no, and the section 7 ceremonies were performed, the marriage is valid. Mulla (notes to Sections 3(g) and 5) explains that clauses (iv) and (v) are based on the old principle of exogamy, and that the Act aims at "uniformity and certainty" on prohibited degrees, which had varied widely across India.
keyPoints: Five conditions: no living spouse, mental capacity, age (21 and 18, completed), no prohibited relationship, no sapinda relationship. Breach of clauses (i), (iv), (v): void (Section 11). Clause (i) is also bigamy (Section 17; now BNS Section 82). Breach of clause (ii): voidable (Section 12(1)(b)). Breach of clause (iii): valid but punishable (Section 18(a)); voidable at the child's option under PCMA Section 3. Custom can save only clauses (iv) and (v), and must govern each party. Sapinda: five generations through the father, three through the mother, counting the person as the first. PCMA 2006: petition before completing two years of attaining majority; offences cognizable and non-bailable; CMRA 1929 repealed. Same gotra, pravara or caste is no bar (Section 5 has none; Section 29(1) saves older marriages). Yamunabai : a bigamous marriage is void, and the woman is not a wife for maintenance; Badshah : except where the man hid his first marriage.

caseLaws.name: Yamunabai Anantrao Adhav v
caseLaws.facts: Anantrao Shivram Adhav (1988) Facts. In June 1974 a woman went through Hindu rites with a man whose first wife was alive. She left after a week, alleging ill-treatment, and in 1976 claimed maintenance as his wife under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Principle. A marriage in breach of Section 5(i) is null and void under Section 11, "void ipso jure", and need not be declared so by a court in advance; Section 12 does not apply to it, and because of Section 4 no earlier law or custom can save it; estoppel cannot defeat the Act, so she was not a "wife" under Section 125. AIR 1988 SC 644 : (1988) 1 SCC 530. Why it matters. It is the leading case on breach of the monogamy condition and on the difference between void and voidable marriages. Badshah v. Urmila Badshah Godse (2013) Facts. A man already married to Shobha married Urmila in 2005 with Hindu rites, hiding his first marriage. She and their daughter claimed maintenance under Section 125 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Principle. Yamunabai applies only where the woman married with full knowledge of the subsisting first marriage; a man who duped her by hiding it cannot take advantage of his own wrong, and for Section 125 she is treated as his wife. (2014) 1 SCC 188 : AIR 2014 SC 869. Why it matters. It limits the harsh result of a void bigamous marriage for a deceived woman.

selfTest.q: 1. What is the result of breaking Section 5(i)?
selfTest.a: The marriage is void under Sections 11 and 17, and bigamy is punishable.

selfTest.q: 2. Is a marriage below the minimum age void under the HMA?
selfTest.a: No. It is valid under the HMA and punishable under Section 18(a). The child party may have it annulled under PCMA Section 3.

selfTest.q: 3. Which clauses can a custom save?
selfTest.a: Clauses (iv) and (v), and only if the custom governs each party.

selfTest.q: 4. A and B share a great-great-grandfather through their fathers. Are they sapindas?
selfTest.a: Yes. The great-great-grandfather is the fifth generation through the father for each of them, which is within the limit.

selfTest.q: 5. Sunil married at 19. By when must he file a petition under PCMA Section 3?
selfTest.a: Before he completes two years of attaining majority, that is, before he turns 20.

selfTest.q: 6. Can a man marry his deceased wife's sister?
selfTest.a: Yes. Relationship by marriage is not a bar unless Section 3(g)(ii) or (iii) names it (Mulla).

legalProvision: Section 5, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Conditions for a Hindu marriage. A marriage may be solemnized between any two Hindus, if the following conditions are fulfilled, namely:— (i) neither party has a spouse living at the time of the marriage; (ii) at the time of the marriage, neither party— (a) is incapable of giving a valid consent to it in consequence of unsoundness of mind; or (b) though capable of giving a valid consent, has been suffering from mental disorder of such a kind or to such an extent as to be unfit for marriage and the procreation of children; or (c) has been subject to recurrent attacks of insanity; (iii) the bridegroom has completed the age of twenty-one years and the bride, the age of eighteen years at the time of the marriage; (iv) the parties are not within the degrees of prohibited relationship unless the custom or usage governing each of them permits of a marriage between the two; (v) the parties are not sapindas of each other, unless the custom or usage governing each of them permits of a marriage between the two;

బేర్ యాక్ట్ నుంచి గమనికలు: క్లాజ్ (ii) ను Act 68 of 1976 ప్రత్యామ్నాయం చేసింది. క్లాజ్ (ii)(c) నుంచి "or epilepsy" అనే పదాలను Act 39 of 1999 తొలగించింది (29 డిసెంబర్ 1999 నుంచి). క్లాజ్ (iii) లో వయస్సులు "eighteen", "fifteen" గా ఉండేవి; Act 2 of 1978 వాటిని ఇరవై ఒకటి, పద్దెనిమిదికి పెంచింది (1 అక్టోబర్ 1978 నుంచి). క్లాజ్ (vi) ని కూడా అదే 1978 చట్టం తొలగించింది.

Section 3(a). the expressions "custom" and "usage" signify any rule which, having been continuously and uniformly observed for a long time, has obtained the force of law among Hindus in any local area, tribe, community, group or family: Provided that the rule is certain and not unreasonable or opposed to public policy; and Provided further that in the case of a rule applicable only to a family it has not been discontinued by the family;

Section 3(f). (i) "sapinda relationship" with reference to any person extends as far as the third generation (inclusive) in the line of ascent through the mother, and the fifth (inclusive) in the line of ascent through the father, the line being traced upwards in each case from the person concerned, who is to be counted as the first generation; (ii) two persons are said to be "sapindas" of each other if one is a lineal ascendant of the other within the limits of sapinda relationship, or if they have a common lineal ascendant who is within the limits of sapinda relationship with reference to each of them;

Section 3(g). "degrees of prohibited relationship"—two persons are said to be within the "degrees of prohibited relationship"— (i) if one is a lineal ascendant of the other; or (ii) if one was the wife or husband of a lineal ascendant or descendant of the other; or (iii) if one was the wife of the brother or of the father's or mother's brother or of the grandfather's or grandmother's brother of the other; or (iv) if the two are brother and sister, uncle and niece, aunt and nephew, or children of brother and sister or of two brothers or of two sisters; Explanation. —For the purposes of clauses (f) and (g), relationship includes— (i) relationship by half or uterine blood as well as by full blood; (ii) illegitimate blood relationship as well as legitimate; (iii) relationship by adoption as well as by blood; and all terms of relationship in those clauses shall be construed accordingly.

Section 11. Void marriages. Any marriage solemnised after the commencement of this Act shall be null and void and may, on a petition presented by either party thereto against the other party, be so declared by a decree of nullity if it contravenes any one of the conditions specified in clauses (i), (iv) and (v) of section 5.

Section 12(1)(b). Voidable marriages. Any marriage solemnised, whether before or after the commencement of this Act, shall be voidable and may be annulled by a decree of nullity on any of the following grounds, namely:— … (b) that the marriage is in contravention of the condition specified in clause (ii) of section 5;

Section 17. Punishment of bigamy. Any marriage between two Hindus solemnized after the commencement of this Act is void if at the date of such marriage either party had a husband or wife living; and the provisions of sections 494 and 495 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (45 of 1860), shall apply accordingly.

Section 18. Punishment for contravention of certain other conditions for a Hindu marriage. Every person who procures a marriage of himself or herself to be solemnized under this Act in contravention of the conditions specified in clauses (iii), (iv), and (v) of section 5 shall be punishable— (a) in the case of contravention of the condition specified in clause (iii) of section 5, with rigorous imprisonment which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to one lakh rupees, or with both. (b) in the case of a contravention of the condition specified in clause (iv) or clause (v) of section 5, with simple imprisonment which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both;
సెక్షన్ 18 క్లాజ్ (a) ను PCMA సెక్షన్ 20 ప్రత్యామ్నాయం చేసింది (30 అక్టోబర్ 2007 నుంచి). సంరక్షకుడి సమ్మతిపై ఉన్న పాత క్లాజ్ (c) ని 1978 లో తొలగించారు.

సరళమైన మాటల్లో: పెళ్లి రోజున ఇద్దరు వ్యక్తులు ఏమి నెరవేర్చాలో సెక్షన్ 5 చెబుతుంది. అందులో వాడిన పదాలను సెక్షన్లు 3(a), (f), (g) వివరిస్తాయి. ఒక షరతు ఉల్లంఘిస్తే ఏమవుతుందో సెక్షన్లు 11, 12, 17, 18 చెబుతాయి. కర్మలు (వేడుకలు) వేరే అవసరం (సెక్షన్ 7, "Ceremonies and Registration" నోట్‌లో ఉంది).
te.meaning:
హిందూ వివాహ షరతులు అంటే ఇద్దరు పక్షాలు వివాహ సమయంలో నెరవేర్చాల్సిన చట్టపరమైన అవసరాలు. వాటిని నెరవేర్చి, సెక్షన్ 7 కోరే కర్మలతో జరిగిన వివాహం చెల్లుబాటయ్యే హిందూ వివాహం. సెక్షన్ 5 పదాల నుంచే మూడు అంశాలు వస్తాయి: "between any two Hindus". ఇద్దరూ చట్టం వర్తించే వ్యక్తులు కావాలి (సెక్షన్ 2). ఒక పక్షం హిందువు కాకపోతే HMA కింద వివాహం సాధ్యం కాదు; వారు ప్రత్యేక వివాహ చట్టం, 1954 కింద పెళ్లి చేసుకోవచ్చు. "at the time of the marriage". ప్రతి షరతును పెళ్లి తేదీన పరీక్షిస్తారు. రెండో పెళ్లి జరిగిన వారం తర్వాత మొదటి భార్య/భర్త మరణించినా, ఆ రెండో పెళ్లి చెల్లుబాటు కాదు. అన్ని షరతులకు ఒకే బరువు లేదు. కొన్నింటి ఉల్లంఘన వివాహాన్ని నాశనం చేస్తుంది (శూన్యం), ఒకదాని ఉల్లంఘన దానిని సవాలుకు తెరుస్తుంది (రద్దు చేయదగినది), వయస్సు షరతు ఉల్లంఘనకు శిక్ష మాత్రమే. దశలవారీ పరీక్షకు Diagram 1 చూడండి. selfTest.q: 1. సెక్షన్ 5(i) ఉల్లంఘన ఫలితం ఏమిటి?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్లు 11, 17 కింద వివాహం శూన్యం; ద్విభార్యత్వం శిక్షార్హం.

selfTest.q: 2. కనీస వయస్సు లోపు జరిగిన వివాహం HMA కింద శూన్యమా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. HMA కింద చెల్లుబాటవుతుంది, సెక్షన్ 18(a) కింద శిక్షార్హం. PCMA సెక్షన్ 3 కింద child పక్షం దానిని రద్దు చేయించుకోవచ్చు.

selfTest.q: 3. ఆచారం ఏ క్లాజులను కాపాడగలదు?
selfTest.a: క్లాజులు (iv), (v); అదీ ఆచారం ప్రతి పక్షాన్నీ నియంత్రిస్తేనే.

selfTest.q: 4. A, B లకు తండ్రుల ద్వారా ఒకే ముత్తాత తండ్రి ఉన్నాడు. వారు సపిండులా?
selfTest.a: అవును. ఇద్దరిలో ప్రతి ఒక్కరికీ ముత్తాత తండ్రి, తండ్రి ద్వారా ఐదవ తరం; అది పరిమితిలోనే ఉంది.

selfTest.q: 5. సునీల్ 19 ఏళ్లకు పెళ్లి చేసుకున్నాడు. PCMA సెక్షన్ 3 కింద ఎప్పటిలోగా పిటిషన్ వేయాలి?

family-law-i-u2-t4.subtitle: Section 7 rites and the saptapadi, and registration of marriage under section 8

en.inOneMinute: Ceremonies make the marriage. Under Section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 (HMA), a Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party. Where those rites include the saptapadi (seven steps taken jointly by the bride and bridegroom before the sacred fire), the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken. Registration only proves the marriage. Section 8 lets the State make rules for entering marriages in a Hindu Marriage Register "for the purpose of facilitating the proof of Hindu marriages". Failure to register does not affect validity (Section 8(5)). Registration cannot create a marriage. In Dolly Rani (2024) the Supreme Court held that a certificate or registration without the ceremonies of Section 7 has no legal consequence; the couple never became husband and wife. Proof in bigamy cases. In Bhaurao (1965) the Supreme Court held that a second marriage is "solemnized" only if performed with the proper ceremonies; without proof of the essential ceremonies there is no bigamy. Alternative. Two Hindus may instead marry, or register an earlier ceremonial marriage, under the Special Marriage Act, 1954.
legalProvision: Section 7, Hindu Marriage Act, 1955. Ceremonies for a Hindu marriage. (1) A Hindu marriage may be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party thereto. (2) Where such rites and ceremonies include the Saptapadi (that is, the taking of seven steps by the bridegroom and the bride jointly before the sacred fire), the marriage becomes complete and binding when the seventh step is taken.

Section 8. Registration of Hindu marriages. (1) For the purpose of facilitating the proof of Hindu marriages, the State Government may make rules providing that the parties to any such marriage may have the particulars relating to their marriage entered in such manner and subject to such conditions as may be prescribed in a Hindu Marriage Register kept for the purpose. (2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), the State Government may, if it is of opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, provide that the entering of the particulars referred to in sub-section (1) shall be compulsory in the State or in any part thereof, whether in all cases or in such cases as may be specified, and where any such direction has been issued, any person contravening any rule made in this behalf shall be punishable with fine which may extend to twenty-five rupees. (3) All rules made under this section shall be laid before the State Legislature, as soon as may be, after they are made. (4) The Hindu Marriage Register shall at all reasonable times be open for inspection, and shall be admissible as evidence of the statements therein contained and certified extracts therefrom shall, on application, be given by the Registrar on payment to him of the prescribed fee. (5) Notwithstanding anything contained in this section, the validity of any Hindu marriage shall in no way be affected by the omission to make the entry.
In simple words:

Section 7(1): the HMA does not list the ceremonies. It accepts the customary rites of the bride's side or the bridegroom's side. Section 7(2): if those rites include the saptapadi , the marriage is complete at the seventh step, not before. Section 8(1)–(3): the State makes the rules for a Hindu Marriage Register. The rules go before the State Legislature. Section 8(2): the State may make the entry compulsory; breaking such a rule is punishable with a fine of up to ₹25 only. Section 8(4): anyone may inspect the Register; its entries are admissible in evidence; certified copies are given on payment of a fee. Section 8(5): an unregistered marriage is still valid.
en.meaning:
Solemnisation . To " solemnize " a marriage is "to celebrate the marriage with proper ceremonies and in due form" ( Bhaurao , adopting the Shorter Oxford Dictionary). "Merely going through certain ceremonies with the intention that the parties be taken to be married, will not make them ceremonies prescribed by law or approved by any established custom." Customary rites and ceremonies. The rites that the custom of the bride's or the bridegroom's community treats as essential. A custom must meet Section 3(a): continuously and uniformly observed for a long time, certain, not unreasonable or opposed to public policy, and, for a family custom, not discontinued. Registration. The entry of the particulars of a marriage in the Hindu Marriage Register kept under the State's rules. It is a record that helps prove the marriage. The topic answers two questions: what ceremonies create a Hindu marriage, and what part registration plays. See Diagram 1 . Diagram 1. The ceremony makes the marriage; registration only records it. flowchart TD A["Customary rites of either party
s. 7(1)"] A --> B{"Do the rites include
saptapadi?"} B -->|"Yes"| C["Marriage complete at the
seventh step: s. 7(2)"] B -->|"No"| D["Marriage complete when the
customary rites are finished"] C --> E["May be entered in the
Hindu Marriage Register: s. 8"] D --> E E --> F["Entry = evidence of the marriage
s. 8(4); no entry: still valid, s. 8(5)"] X["No rites at all,
only a certificate"] --> Y["No Hindu marriage;
registration has no effect
(Dolly Rani)"] Text description The parties perform the customary rites of either side under section 7(1). If the saptapadi is part of the rites, the marriage is complete at the seventh step under section 7(2). The marriage may then be entered in the Hindu Marriage Register under section 8. The entry is evidence of the marriage; it does not create or cure the marriage. If no rites were performed, a certificate or registration has no effect (Dolly Rani).
keyPoints: Section 7: customary rites of either party; the Act prescribes no fixed ceremony. Saptapadi: where part of the rites, the marriage is complete at the seventh step. Essential rites in a ceremonial marriage: invocation before the sacred fire and saptapadi, unless a proved custom changes them ( Bhaurao ; Mulla s. 437). Custom must be proved by definite evidence, not by what was done at one wedding. Bigamy needs a properly solemnized second marriage; admission is not proof ( Priya Bala Ghosh ). Section 8(5): non-registration does not affect validity; fine up to ₹25 where compulsory. Registration does not create a marriage ( Dolly Rani ). Seema : marriages of all religions to be compulsorily registrable; registration has great evidentiary value. Special Marriage Act, 1954: thirty days' notice, three witnesses, conclusive certificate; an earlier marriage can be registered under Sections 15 to 18.

caseLaws.name: Bhaurao Shankar Lokhande v
caseLaws.facts: State of Maharashtra (1965) Facts. Bhaurao married Indubai in about 1956 and, while she was alive, went through a "Gandharva" marriage with Kamlabai in February 1962 by an exchange of garlands and touching of foreheads, without homa or saptapadi. He was convicted under Section 494 IPC and his brother of abetment . Principle. A marriage is "solemnized" only when celebrated with proper ceremonies and in due form; invocation before the sacred fire and saptapadi are essential even in a Gandharva marriage unless a proved custom has changed them, and a practice of five or seven years is not a custom under Section 3(a); the convictions were set aside. AIR 1965 SC 1564 : (1965) 2 SCR 837. Why it matters. It defines "solemnize" and sets what must be proved to show a marriage, especially a second marriage in a bigamy case. Priya Bala Ghosh v. Suresh Chandra Ghosh (1971) Facts. A wife prosecuted her husband for bigamy. The courts found no evidence that homa and saptapadi, essential rites in the parties' community, were performed at the second marriage; she relied on his earlier admission that he had married again. Principle. The prosecution must prove that the second marriage was duly performed with the essential rites of the parties' law and custom; an admission of marriage by the accused is no evidence of the marriage in a bigamy case. Appeal dismissed. [1971] 3 SCR 961 : AIR 1971 SC 1153. Why it matters. It confirms Bhaurao and shows how strictly the ceremonies must be proved. Seema v. Ashwani Kumar (2006) Facts. In a transfer petition the Supreme Court noticed that many people deny their marriages because there is no official record. It heard the States, the Union Territories and the National Commission for Women on registration. Principle. Registration is not per se proof of a valid marriage but has great evidentiary value; marriages of all citizens of India, of all religions, should be compulsorily registrable in the State where solemnized; the States must notify the procedure within three months. Decided 14 February 2006. Why it matters. It explains the place of registration and led to compulsory registration rules. Dolly Rani v. Manish Kumar Chanchal (2024) Facts. Two commercial pilots, engaged on 7 March 2021, obtained on 7 July 2021 a certificate from a society and a registration certificate under the Uttar Pradesh Marriage Registration Rules, 2017, without any ceremony; the families fixed a ceremony for 25 October 2022 that was never held. Principle. Without the ceremonies of Section 7 there is no Hindu marriage, and registration under Section 8 confers no status; on their joint application under Article 142 the Court declared both certificates null and void and quashed the divorce, maintenance and criminal cases between them. 2024 INSC 355. Why it matters. Registration only proves a marriage that has taken place; it cannot create one.

selfTest.q: 1. When is a marriage with saptapadi complete?
selfTest.a: When the seventh step is taken (Section 7(2)).

selfTest.q: 2. Does failure to register invalidate a Hindu marriage?
selfTest.a: No. Section 8(5), even where registration is compulsory.

selfTest.q: 3. Which case held that a certificate without ceremonies has no effect?
selfTest.a: Dolly Rani v. Manish Kumar Chanchal (2024).

selfTest.q: 4. In a bigamy case, can the second marriage be proved by the accused's own admission?
selfTest.a: No. The ceremonies must be proved ( Priya Bala Ghosh , following Bhaurao ).

selfTest.q: 5. Witnesses say a priest was not needed at a Gandharva wedding in their community. Does that prove a custom dispensing with saptapadi?
selfTest.a: No. Evidence of what was done is not evidence of the custom ( Bhaurao ).

selfTest.q: 6. What is the evidentiary value of a certificate under the Special Marriage Act?
selfTest.a: It is conclusive evidence that the marriage was solemnized under that Act (Section 13(2)).

సెక్షన్ 7(1): HMA వేడుకల జాబితా ఇవ్వదు. వధువు వైపు లేదా వరుడి వైపు ఆచార కర్మలను అంగీకరిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 7(2): ఆ కర్మల్లో సప్తపది ఉంటే, ఏడవ అడుగుతో వివాహం పూర్తవుతుంది, అంతకుముందు కాదు. సెక్షన్ 8(1)–(3): హిందూ వివాహ రిజిస్టర్ కోసం రాష్ట్రం నియమాలు చేస్తుంది. నియమాలు రాష్ట్ర శాసనసభ ముందు ఉంచాలి. సెక్షన్ 8(2): రాష్ట్రం నమోదును తప్పనిసరి చేయవచ్చు; అలాంటి నియమాన్ని ఉల్లంఘిస్తే ₹25 వరకు జరిమానా మాత్రమే. సెక్షన్ 8(4): ఎవరైనా రిజిస్టర్‌ను తనిఖీ చేయవచ్చు; దాని నమోదులు సాక్ష్యంగా ఆమోదయోగ్యం; ఫీజు చెల్లిస్తే సర్టిఫైడ్ కాపీలు ఇస్తారు. సెక్షన్ 8(5): రిజిస్టర్ కాని వివాహం కూడా చెల్లుబాటవుతుంది.

వివాహ నిర్వహణ (Solemnisation) . వివాహాన్ని " solemnize " చేయడం అంటే "to celebrate the marriage with proper ceremonies and in due form" ( Bhaurao , Shorter Oxford Dictionary ఆధారంగా). "Merely going through certain ceremonies with the intention that the parties be taken to be married, will not make them ceremonies prescribed by law or approved by any established custom." ఆచార కర్మలు, వేడుకలు. వధువు లేదా వరుడి సమాజపు ఆచారం ముఖ్యమైనవిగా భావించే కర్మలు. ఆచారం సెక్షన్ 3(a) ని నెరవేర్చాలి: చాలా కాలంగా నిరంతరంగా, ఒకే విధంగా పాటించబడాలి; నిశ్చితంగా ఉండాలి; అసమంజసంగా లేదా ప్రజా విధానానికి విరుద్ధంగా ఉండకూడదు; కుటుంబ ఆచారం అయితే నిలిపివేయబడి ఉండకూడదు. రిజిస్ట్రేషన్. రాష్ట్ర నియమాల కింద ఉంచే హిందూ వివాహ రిజిస్టర్‌లో వివాహ వివరాల నమోదు. ఇది వివాహాన్ని రుజువు చేయడానికి సహాయపడే రికార్డు. ఈ అంశం రెండు ప్రశ్నలకు జవాబిస్తుంది: ఏ వేడుకలు హిందూ వివాహాన్ని సృష్టిస్తాయి, రిజిస్ట్రేషన్ పాత్ర ఏమిటి.
