Section 88: failure to comply with a direction of the Central Authority under section 20 or 21 is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs 20 lakh, or both. Section 89: a false or misleading advertisement is punishable with imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh, and for each later offence imprisonment up to five years and fine up to Rs 50 lakh. Section 90: selling products containing an adulterant is punishable, with heavier punishment as the injury grows. Section 91: the same for spurious goods. Section 92: a court may take cognizance offences under sections 88 and 89 only on a complaint by the Central Authority or an officer it authorises. Section 93: an officer who makes a vexatious search or seizure is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to Rs 10,000, or both.
en.meaning: Civil liability is a duty to repair the consumer's loss by giving relief or money. Criminal liability is a duty to answer to the State for an offence and to suffer the punishment the law lays down. One act, such as selling unsafe food, can lead to both.
keyPoints: Civil track: section 39 relief and product liability (sections 82 to 87). Section 72: one month to three years, fine Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh. Section 89: up to two years and Rs 10 lakh; later offence up to five years and Rs 50 lakh. Sections 90 and 91: punishment grows with the injury; death carries at least seven years. Section 92: cognizance of sections 88 and 89 only on the Central Authority's complaint.

caseLaws.name: Indian Medical Association v
caseLaws.facts: V.P. Shantha (1995) Facts. Conflicting rulings on whether a doctor's or hospital's work is service under the 1986 Act. Principle. Medical work for a fee is service. The patient can seek civil relief before the consumer forum. Significance. Civil liability of professionals under the Act. Spring Meadows Hospital v. Harjot Ahluwalia (1998) Facts. A nurse injected a minor patient without a sensitivity test, leaving him in a vegetative state. Principle. Both the child and the parents are consumers who can each be compensated on their own head of loss. Significance. Compensation as civil liability.

caseLaws.name: No judgment in this collection is relied on for the criminal provisions
caseLaws.facts: They rest on the text of the Act.

selfTest.q: 1. Which section punishes disobeying a Commission's order?
selfTest.a: Section 72. 2. Who can start a prosecution under sections 88 and 89? The Central Authority or an officer it authorises (section 92). 3. What is the minimum punishment if adulterated goods cause death? Imprisonment of at least seven years and fine of at least Rs 10 lakh (section 90(1)(d)).

legalProvision: సెక్షన్ 39: లోపం, తక్కువతనం లేదా అన్యాయ వాణిజ్య పద్ధతి రుజువైతే District Commission లోపం తొలగింపు, మార్పిడి, వాపసు, పరిహారం లేదా ఇతర ఉపశమనం ఆదేశిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్లు 82 నుండి 87: Product liability. లోపభూయిష్ఠ ఉత్పత్తి వల్ల కలిగిన హానికి తయారీదారు, product service provider లేదా product seller బాధ్యులు. సెక్షన్ 72: Commission ఉత్తర్వును పాటించకపోతే ఒక నెల నుండి మూడేళ్ల జైలు శిక్ష, లేదా రూ. 25,000 నుండి రూ. 1 లక్ష జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ. సెక్షన్ 88: సెక్షన్ 20 లేదా 21 కింద Central Authority ఆదేశాన్ని పాటించకపోతే ఆరు నెలల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, లేదా రూ. 20 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ. సెక్షన్ 89: తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటనకు రెండేళ్ల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, రూ. 10 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా. ప్రతి తదుపరి నేరానికి ఐదేళ్ల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, రూ. 50 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా. సెక్షన్ 90: adulterant ఉన్న ఉత్పత్తులు అమ్మడం శిక్షార్హం. గాయం పెరిగే కొద్దీ శిక్ష పెరుగుతుంది. సెక్షన్ 91: నకిలీ వస్తువులకు ఇదే వర్తిస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 92: సెక్షన్లు 88, 89 కింద నేరాలపై Central Authority లేదా అది అధికారమిచ్చిన అధికారి ఫిర్యాదు చేస్తేనే కోర్టు cognizance తీసుకోవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 93: ఏ కారణమూ లేకుండా వేధించే సోదా లేదా స్వాధీనం చేసిన అధికారికి ఒక సంవత్సరం వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, లేదా రూ. 10,000 వరకు జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ.
te.meaning: Civil బాధ్యత అంటే ఉపశమనం లేదా డబ్బు ఇచ్చి వినియోగదారు నష్టాన్ని భర్తీ చేసే బాధ్యత. Criminal బాధ్యత అంటే నేరానికి రాజ్యానికి సమాధానం చెప్పి, చట్టం విధించిన శిక్షను అనుభవించే బాధ్యత. ప్రమాదకర ఆహారం అమ్మడం వంటి ఒకే చర్య రెండింటికీ దారి తీయవచ్చు.

selfTest.q: 1. Commission ఉత్తర్వు ధిక్కారాన్ని ఏ సెక్షన్ శిక్షిస్తుంది?
selfTest.a: సెక్షన్ 72. 2. సెక్షన్లు 88, 89 కింద ప్రాసిక్యూషన్ ఎవరు ప్రారంభించవచ్చు? Central Authority లేదా అది అధికారమిచ్చిన అధికారి (సెక్షన్ 92). 3. కల్తీ వస్తువులు మరణానికి కారణమైతే కనీస శిక్ష ఏమిటి? కనీసం ఏడేళ్ల జైలు శిక్ష, కనీసం రూ. 10 లక్షల జరిమానా (సెక్షన్ 90(1)(d)).

law-of-torts-u5-t19.subtitle: Settling consumer disputes by agreement: mediation under the 2019 Act and the place of other alternative dispute resolution

en.inOneMinute: Alternative dispute resolution (ADR) means settling a dispute without a full trial. The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 builds one ADR method into the Commissions: mediation. A Commission can send the parties to mediation if a settlement looks possible, and the parties must agree in writing. In exams, this topic is asked as a short note on ADR and consumer disputes, or on mediation under the Act. The usual trap is to think that mediation is compulsory. It needs the written consent of both parties.
legalProvision: Section 37: at the first hearing or later, if elements of a settlement acceptable to the parties appear, the District Commission may ask the parties to give written consent within five days to mediation under Chapter V. On consent, it refers the matter within five days. prescribed cases are excluded. Section 74: a consumer mediation cell is set up with each District and State Commission by the State Government, and with the National Commission and its regional Benches by the Central Government. Section 75: each Commission prepares a panel of mediators on the recommendation of a selection committee of its President and a member. The panel is valid for five years. Section 79: mediation is held in the cell, and the mediator is guided by the principles of natural justice. Section 80: a settlement is written down and signed by the parties, and the mediator sends it with a report to the Commission. Section 81: the Commission passes an order recording the settlement within seven days. Section 100: the Act is in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law in force. Section 2(25): mediation means the process by which a mediator mediates the consumer disputes. Section 41 (third proviso ):
en.meaning: ADR covers methods such as negotiation, mediation, conciliation, arbitration and Lok Adalats. In these methods, the parties, with the help of a neutral person or body, reach a result outside the ordinary court process. In the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the method given a place inside the Act is mediation. A mediator helps the parties reach their own agreement and does not decide the dispute.
keyPoints: Mediation needs written consent of the parties within five days (section 37). A consumer mediation cell is attached to each Commission (section 74). The panel of mediators is valid for five years (section 75). The Commission records a settlement within seven days (section 81). If mediation fails, the Commission hears all issues. Mediation ends in three months from the first appearance unless extended (Regulation 11(2)).

caseLaws.name: This topic rests on the text of the Act
caseLaws.facts: No judgment in this collection is relied on for it.

selfTest.q: 1. Is mediation compulsory under the 2019 Act?
selfTest.a: No. The parties must consent in writing. 2. Within how many days must the Commission record a settlement? Seven days from receiving the settlement report (section 81). 3. What happens if mediation fails? The Commission continues to hear all the issues.

legalProvision: సెక్షన్ 37: మొదటి విచారణలో లేదా తర్వాత, పక్షాలకు ఆమోదయోగ్యమైన రాజీ అంశాలు కనిపిస్తే, District Commission Chapter V కింద mediation కు ఐదు రోజుల్లో రాతపూర్వక సమ్మతి ఇవ్వమని పక్షాలను కోరవచ్చు. సమ్మతి ఇస్తే ఐదు రోజుల్లో వ్యవహారాన్ని పంపుతుంది. నిర్దేశించిన కేసులు మినహాయింపు. సెక్షన్ 74: ప్రతి District, State Commission కు రాష్ట్ర ప్రభుత్వం, National Commission, దాని ప్రాంతీయ Benches కు కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం consumer mediation cell ఏర్పాటు చేస్తాయి. సెక్షన్ 75: ప్రతి Commission తన President, ఒక సభ్యునితో కూడిన selection committee సిఫారసుపై మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్ తయారు చేస్తుంది. ప్యానెల్ ఐదేళ్లు చెల్లుబాటు అవుతుంది. సెక్షన్ 79: Mediation cell లో జరుగుతుంది, మధ్యవర్తి natural justice సూత్రాలను అనుసరిస్తాడు. సెక్షన్ 80: పరిష్కారాన్ని రాసి పక్షాలు సంతకం చేస్తాయి. మధ్యవర్తి దాన్ని నివేదికతో Commission కు పంపుతాడు. సెక్షన్ 81: Commission ఏడు రోజుల్లో పరిష్కారాన్ని నమోదు చేస్తూ ఉత్తర్వు ఇస్తుంది. సెక్షన్ 100: చట్టం అమలులో ఉన్న ఇతర చట్టానికి అదనం, దాని నుండి తీసివేత కాదు. సెక్షన్ 2(25): mediation అంటే mediator వినియోగదారుల వివాదాలను మధ్యవర్తిత్వంతో పరిష్కరించే ప్రక్రియ. సెక్షన్ 41 (మూడో proviso ):
te.meaning: ADR లో negotiation, mediation, conciliation, arbitration, Lok Adalat వంటి పద్ధతులు ఉంటాయి. వీటిలో పక్షాలు తటస్థ వ్యక్తి లేదా సంస్థ సహాయంతో సాధారణ కోర్టు ప్రక్రియ వెలుపల ఫలితాన్ని సాధిస్తాయి. Consumer Protection Act, 2019 లో చట్టంలోనే స్థానం పొందిన పద్ధతి mediation. మధ్యవర్తి పక్షాలు తమ ఒప్పందానికి చేరడానికి సహాయం చేస్తాడు, వివాదాన్ని తానే నిర్ణయించడు.

selfTest.q: 1. 2019 చట్టం కింద mediation తప్పనిసరా?
selfTest.a: కాదు. పక్షాలు రాతపూర్వకంగా సమ్మతించాలి. 2. Commission పరిష్కారాన్ని ఎన్ని రోజుల్లో నమోదు చేయాలి? Settlement report అందిన ఏడు రోజుల్లో (సెక్షన్ 81). 3. Mediation విఫలమైతే ఏమవుతుంది? Commission అన్ని అంశాలను విచారణ కొనసాగిస్తుంది.

law-of-torts-u5-t20.subtitle: What counts as a misleading advertisement, and the penalties the Central Authority and the courts can impose

en.inOneMinute: The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 deals with misleading advertisements on two levels. The Central Consumer Protection Authority can order the advertisement to stop and can impose a money penalty on the maker and the endorser. A court can also punish the manufacturer or service provider with imprisonment and fine. In exams, this topic is asked as a short note on misleading advertisements and their penalties. The usual trap is to mix the Authority's penalty under section 21 with the court's punishment under section 89.
legalProvision: Section 2(28): a misleading advertisement is one that falsely describes a product or service or gives a false guarantee. It is also one that is likely to mislead consumers about nature, substance, quantity or quality, or that conveys a representation that would be an unfair trade practice. An advertisement that deliberately conceals important information is misleading too. Section 2(18): an endorsement is a message, statement, demonstration, or depiction of a name, likeness or seal that makes the consumer believe it reflects the opinion, finding or experience of the person endorsing. Section 21: the Central Authority may direct discontinuance or modification of the advertisement, impose a penalty, and bar an endorser. Section 89: a manufacturer or service provider who causes a false or misleading advertisement prejudicial to consumers is punishable with imprisonment up to two years and fine up to Rs 10 lakh. For each later offence, imprisonment up to five years and fine up to Rs 50 lakh. Section 92: a court takes cognizance of an offence under section 88 or section 89 only on a complaint by the Central Authority or an officer it authorises. Section 88: failing to comply with a direction of the Central Authority under section 20 or 21 is punishable with imprisonment up to six months, or fine up to Rs 20 lakh, or both. Section 24: a person aggrieved by an order of the Central Authority under section 20 or 21 may appeal to the National Commission within 30 days of receiving the order. Section 39(1)(l) and (n): a Commission deciding a complaint may order a corrective advertisement, at the cost of the opposite party, to neutralise a misleading advertisement. It may also order the party to stop issuing misleading advertisements. Section 93: an officer who searches or seizes under section 22 knowing there are no reasonable grounds is punishable with imprisonment up to one year, or fine up to Rs 10,000, or both.
en.meaning: A misleading advertisement is not limited to a plain lie. It includes an advertisement that is likely to mislead, one that makes a promise that would be an unfair trade practice, and one that hides important information on purpose. An endorser is the person whose name, face, message or seal is used to lend credit to the advertisement.
keyPoints: Misleading advertisement is defined in section 2(28). Authority penalty: up to Rs 10 lakh; later up to Rs 50 lakh (section 21). Endorser bar: up to one year; later up to three years. Endorser's defence: due diligence (section 21(5)). Court punishment: up to two years and Rs 10 lakh; later up to five years and Rs 50 lakh (section 89).

caseLaws.name: This topic rests on the text of the Act
caseLaws.facts: No judgment in this collection is relied on for it.

selfTest.q: 1. How long can an endorser be barred for a first contravention?
selfTest.a: Up to one year (section 21(3)). 2. What defence does an endorser have? He exercised due diligence to verify the claims (section 21(5)). 3. Who can complain for an offence under section 89? The Central Authority or an officer it authorises (section 92).

legalProvision: సెక్షన్ 2(28): ఉత్పత్తిని లేదా సేవను తప్పుగా వర్ణించే, తప్పుడు హామీ ఇచ్చే, స్వభావం, సారం, పరిమాణం లేదా నాణ్యత గురించి వినియోగదారులను తప్పుదారి పట్టించే అవకాశం ఉన్న, అన్యాయ వాణిజ్య పద్ధతి అయ్యే ప్రాతినిధ్యం తెలిపే, లేదా ముఖ్యమైన సమాచారాన్ని ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా దాచే ప్రకటన తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన. సెక్షన్ 2(18): Endorsement అంటే ఆమోదించే వ్యక్తి అభిప్రాయం, కనుగొన్నది లేదా అనుభవాన్ని ప్రతిబింబిస్తుందని వినియోగదారు నమ్మేలా చేసే సందేశం, ప్రకటన, ప్రదర్శన, లేదా పేరు, రూపం, ముద్ర చిత్రణ. సెక్షన్ 21: ప్రకటనను ఆపమని లేదా మార్చమని Central Authority ఆదేశించవచ్చు, జరిమానా విధించవచ్చు, endorser పై నిషేధం విధించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 89: వినియోగదారుల ప్రయోజనానికి హానికరమైన తప్పుడు లేదా తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన చేయించిన తయారీదారు లేదా సేవా ప్రదాతకు రెండేళ్ల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, రూ. 10 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా. ప్రతి తదుపరి నేరానికి ఐదేళ్ల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, రూ. 50 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా. సెక్షన్ 92: సెక్షన్ 88 లేదా సెక్షన్ 89 నేరంపై Central Authority లేదా అది అధికారమిచ్చిన అధికారి ఫిర్యాదు చేస్తేనే కోర్టు cognizance తీసుకుంటుంది. సెక్షన్ 88: సెక్షన్ 20 లేదా 21 కింద Central Authority ఆదేశాన్ని పాటించకపోతే ఆరు నెలల వరకు జైలు శిక్ష, లేదా రూ. 20 లక్షల వరకు జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ. సెక్షన్ 24: సెక్షన్ 20 లేదా 21 కింద Central Authority ఇచ్చిన ఉత్తర్వుతో బాధపడిన వ్యక్తి, ఉత్తర్వు అందిన 30 రోజుల్లో National Commission కు అప్పీలు చేయవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 39(1)(l), (n): ఫిర్యాదును నిర్ణయించే Commission, తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన ప్రభావాన్ని తొలగించడానికి ప్రత్యర్థి ఖర్చుతో corrective advertisement ఇవ్వమని ఆదేశించవచ్చు. తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటనలు ఆపమని కూడా ఆదేశించవచ్చు. సెక్షన్ 93: సెక్షన్ 22 కింద సోదా లేదా స్వాధీనం చేసిన అధికారికి సరైన కారణాలు లేవని తెలిసి అలా చేస్తే, ఒక సంవత్సరం వరకు జైలు, లేదా రూ. 10,000 వరకు జరిమానా, లేదా రెండూ విధించవచ్చు.
te.meaning: తప్పుదారి పట్టించే ప్రకటన అంటే కేవలం స్పష్టమైన అబద్ధం మాత్రమే కాదు. తప్పుదారి పట్టించే అవకాశం ఉన్న ప్రకటన, అన్యాయ వాణిజ్య పద్ధతి అయ్యే వాగ్దానం చేసే ప్రకటన, ముఖ్యమైన సమాచారాన్ని ఉద్దేశపూర్వకంగా దాచే ప్రకటన కూడా ఇందులో ఉంటాయి. Endorser అంటే ప్రకటనకు విశ్వసనీయత ఇవ్వడానికి తన పేరు, ముఖం, సందేశం లేదా ముద్ర వాడబడిన వ్యక్తి.

selfTest.q: 1. మొదటి ఉల్లంఘనకు endorser ను ఎంతకాలం నిషేధించవచ్చు?
selfTest.a: ఒక సంవత్సరం వరకు (సెక్షన్ 21(3)). 2. Endorser కు ఏ రక్షణ ఉంటుంది? వాదనలను ధృవీకరించడంలో due diligence చూపడం (సెక్షన్ 21(5)). 3. సెక్షన్ 89 నేరంపై ఎవరు ఫిర్యాదు చేయవచ్చు? Central Authority లేదా అది అధికారమిచ్చిన అధికారి (సెక్షన్ 92).

law-of-torts-u5-t21.subtitle: Chapter V of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019: the mediation cell, the panel of mediators, their duties and how a settlement becomes an order

en.inOneMinute: Chapter V of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (sections 74 to 81) sets up mediation inside the consumer forums. Each Commission has a consumer mediation cell with a panel of mediators valid for five years. A mediator must disclose any interest, and the Commission records the settlement within seven days. In exams, this topic is asked as a long answer on the empanelment, appointment and duties of mediators and the settlement of disputes. The usual trap is to confuse empanelment, which creates the panel, with nomination, which picks one mediator for one dispute.
legalProvision: Section 37: reference to mediation by the District Commission, with written consent of the parties within five days. Section 74: establishment of the consumer mediation cell. Section 75: empanelment of mediators. Section 76: nomination of mediators from the panel. Section 77: duty of the mediator to disclose certain facts. Section 78: replacement of a mediator. Section 79: procedure for mediation. Section 80: settlement through mediation. Section 81: recording of the settlement and passing of the order. Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020: made by the Central Government (G.S.R. 450(E), 15 July 2020, in force from 20 July 2020). They cover the cell, the selection committee, excluded matters, refund of fee and the effect of a settlement. Consumer Protection (Mediation) Regulations, 2020: made by the National Commission (24 July 2020). They cover empanelment, fee, training, code of conduct, procedure, confidentiality and reports.
en.meaning: Mediation is a way of settling a dispute in which a neutral mediator helps the parties reach an agreement. Empanelment means putting a person on the approved panel of mediators. Nomination means choosing a mediator from that panel for a particular dispute.
keyPoints: A mediation cell is attached to every Commission (section 74). The panel is valid for five years, on the recommendation of a selection committee (section 75). The mediator must disclose any interest or doubt about independence (section 77). The mediator is guided by natural justice (section 79). The Commission records the settlement within seven days (section 81). Mediation ends in three months from the first appearance unless extended (Regulation 11(2)). The mediator cannot impose a settlement, and the proceedings are confidential (Regulations 12 and 13). The complainant gets the full application fee back if a settlement is reached (Rule 5).

caseLaws.name: This topic rests on the text of the Act
caseLaws.facts: No judgment in this collection is relied on for it.

selfTest.q: 1. For how long is the panel of mediators valid?
selfTest.a: Five years, with re-empanelment possible (section 75(3)). 2. Who recommends the panel of mediators? A selection committee of the President and a member of the Commission (section 75(1)). 3. What does a mediator send to the Commission after a settlement? The signed agreement with a settlement report (section 80(2)). 4. Within what time must mediation be completed? Three months from the first appearance before the mediator, unless the Commission extends it (Regulation 11(2)). 5. Which matters are not referred to mediation? Those listed in Rule 4, such as medical negligence causing grievous injury or death, and cases of serious fraud or forgery.

legalProvision: సెక్షన్ 37: ఐదు రోజుల్లో పక్షాల రాతపూర్వక సమ్మతితో District Commission mediation కు పంపడం. సెక్షన్ 74: Consumer mediation cell ఏర్పాటు. సెక్షన్ 75: మధ్యవర్తుల empanelment. సెక్షన్ 76: ప్యానెల్ నుండి మధ్యవర్తుల nomination. సెక్షన్ 77: కొన్ని వాస్తవాలను వెల్లడించే మధ్యవర్తి విధి. సెక్షన్ 78: మధ్యవర్తి మార్పు. సెక్షన్ 79: Mediation విధానం. సెక్షన్ 80: Mediation ద్వారా పరిష్కారం. సెక్షన్ 81: పరిష్కారం నమోదు, ఉత్తర్వు జారీ. Consumer Protection (Mediation) Rules, 2020: కేంద్ర ప్రభుత్వం చేసిన నియమాలు (G.S.R. 450(E), 15 జూలై 2020; 20 జూలై 2020 నుండి అమలు). Cell, selection committee, మినహాయించిన అంశాలు, ఫీజు వాపసు, పరిష్కారం ప్రభావాన్ని ఇవి చెబుతాయి. Consumer Protection (Mediation) Regulations, 2020: National Commission చేసిన నిబంధనలు (24 జూలై 2020). Empanelment, ఫీజు, శిక్షణ, ప్రవర్తనా నియమావళి, విధానం, గోప్యత, నివేదికలను ఇవి చెబుతాయి.
te.meaning: Mediation అంటే తటస్థ మధ్యవర్తి పక్షాలు ఒప్పందానికి చేరడానికి సహాయం చేసే వివాద పరిష్కార పద్ధతి. Empanelment అంటే ఒక వ్యక్తిని ఆమోదించిన మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్‌లో చేర్చడం. Nomination అంటే ఆ ప్యానెల్ నుండి ఒక నిర్దిష్ట వివాదానికి మధ్యవర్తిని ఎంచుకోవడం.

selfTest.q: 1. మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్ ఎంతకాలం చెల్లుబాటు అవుతుంది?
selfTest.a: ఐదేళ్లు, re-empanelment సాధ్యం (సెక్షన్ 75(3)). 2. మధ్యవర్తుల ప్యానెల్‌ను ఎవరు సిఫారసు చేస్తారు? Commission President, ఒక సభ్యునితో కూడిన selection committee (సెక్షన్ 75(1)). 3. పరిష్కారం తర్వాత మధ్యవర్తి Commission కు ఏం పంపుతాడు? సంతకం చేసిన ఒప్పందాన్ని settlement report తో (సెక్షన్ 80(2)). 4. Mediation ఎంత సమయంలో పూర్తి కావాలి? మధ్యవర్తి ముందు మొదటి హాజరు నుండి మూడు నెలలు, Commission పొడిగిస్తే తప్ప (Regulation 11(2)). 5. ఏ అంశాలను mediation కు పంపరు? Rule 4 లో ఉన్నవి: తీవ్రమైన గాయం లేదా మరణానికి దారితీసిన వైద్య నిర్లక్ష్యం, తీవ్రమైన మోసం లేదా ఫోర్జరీ కేసులు వంటివి.

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
Before any consumer-specific statute existed, which tort was the primary remedy available to a consumer injured by a defective product or careless service?

Explanation. Before consumer-specific legislation, an injured consumer's only real remedy was the tort of negligence — proving a duty of care, breach, and resulting damage.

What barrier did the doctrine of privity of contract traditionally create for an injured consumer?

Explanation. Privity of contract meant a buyer generally had no claim against a manufacturer or other party they had no direct contract with, even if that party's carelessness caused the harm.

In Donoghue v. Stevenson, what did the House of Lords hold about a manufacturer's duty of care?

Explanation. The House of Lords held that a manufacturer's duty of care to the ultimate consumer exists independently of contract, removing privity as a bar to a negligence claim.

In Cassidy v. Ministry of Health, the Ministry relied on an older, narrower view of hospital liability. Which test did the Court of Appeal move away from?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
What best describes 'consumerism'?

Explanation. Consumerism is a collective, organised movement — through associations, advocacy, and legislative lobbying — not merely individual shopping caution.

Why couldn't ordinary tort remedies alone correct market-wide consumer harms such as adulteration or false advertising?

Explanation. Tort remedies compensate one injured consumer at a time, long after harm occurs, and only if that consumer can afford to litigate — inadequate for correcting market-wide problems.

The doctrine of caveat emptor means

Explanation. Caveat emptor, 'let the buyer beware', historically placed the responsibility of examining goods before purchase on the buyer, with limited seller disclosure duties.

Consumerism pushed the law towards a philosophy closer to which principle?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
Under section 34(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, the District Commission hears complaints where the consideration paid does not exceed:

Explanation. Section 34(1) fixes the limit at Rs 1 crore and lets the Central Government prescribe another value. The 2021 Rules prescribed Rs 50 lakh. Section 107 repealed the Consumer Protection Act, 1986.

What is the single most significant structural innovation of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?

Explanation. The CCPA is a dedicated regulatory body that can investigate and act on its own initiative, without waiting for an individual consumer complaint — something the 1986 Act had no equivalent of.

How does the 2019 Act treat product liability differently from the position under the 1986 Act?

Explanation. The 2019 Act, for the first time, gives product liability its own dedicated statutory chapter with defined standards, instead of requiring reliance purely on common-law negligence.

Which of the following transactions did the 2019 Act expressly bring within the definition of 'consumer', closing a gap under the 1986 Act?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
Under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, a 'consumer' is a person who buys goods or avails a service for consideration, but excludes a person acting for a

Explanation. A person who buys goods or avails a service for a 'commercial purpose' is excluded from the definition of 'consumer' under Section 2(7).

Which of the following buyers is NOT excluded from being a 'consumer', despite the commercial-purpose exclusion?

Explanation. The Act expressly carves out goods bought and used exclusively for earning one's livelihood through self-employment from the commercial-purpose exclusion.

Besides the person who actually pays for goods or a service, who else does the definition of 'consumer' include?

Explanation. The definition extends to a user of goods with the buyer's approval and a beneficiary of a service with the hirer's approval, even if they did not personally pay.

How many consumer rights does the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 expressly recognise?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
Under Section 2(10) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, 'defect' applies to

Explanation. 'Defect' under Section 2(10) is defined specifically in relation to goods or products.

A trader advertises a claim about a product's performance that the product does not actually meet, even though no separate law or contract required that specific standard. Can this still amount to a 'defect'?

Explanation. 'Defect' under Section 2(10) expressly includes a shortfall against a standard 'claimed by the trader in any manner whatsoever' about the goods.

Under Section 2(11), 'deficiency' in a service expressly includes

Explanation. Section 2(11) expressly writes negligence and deliberate withholding of relevant information into the definition of 'deficiency'.

How does proof of a defect in goods usually differ from proof of a deficiency in a service?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
'Unfair trade practice' under Section 2(47) primarily targets

Explanation. Unfair trade practice targets deceptive or unfair methods used to promote sale/use/supply, such as false representations and false guarantees.

Which of the following is expressly listed as an unfair trade practice under the 2019 Act?

Explanation. Section 2(47)(ix) lists disclosing personal information given in confidence by the consumer, unless the disclosure is made in accordance with law.

'Restrictive trade practice' under Section 2(41) primarily targets

Explanation. Restrictive trade practice centres on distorting the market's ordinary functioning (price, delivery, supply), harming consumers collectively.

What is a 'tie-in arrangement'?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
How many tiers of Consumer Protection Councils does the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 establish?

Explanation. The Act establishes a three-tier structure of Consumer Protection Councils — Central, State, and District.

Who chairs the Central Consumer Protection Council?

Explanation. The Central Consumer Protection Council is chaired by the Union Minister in charge of Consumer Affairs.

Who chairs the District Consumer Protection Council?

Explanation. The District Consumer Protection Council is chaired by the District Collector or an equivalent officer.

What is the core object of every Consumer Protection Council, regardless of level?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
Under which section of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 is the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) established?

Explanation. Section 10 empowers the Central Government to establish the CCPA by notification.

What is the key difference between the CCPA and the District/State/National Commissions?

Explanation. The CCPA's mandate is regulatory/preventive protection of consumers as a class, distinct from the Commissions' role of adjudicating individual complaints.

On what basis can the CCPA initiate an inquiry or investigation?

Explanation. The CCPA can act suo motu (on its own initiative), on a complaint, or on the direction of the Central Government.

Who heads the CCPA's Investigation Wing?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
What is the fundamental character of civil liability under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019?

Explanation. Civil liability under the Act is compensatory — refund, replacement, compensation, and discontinuation orders — not punitive.

Can civil liability and criminal liability under the Act arise from the same underlying conduct?

Explanation. Civil liability (before a Commission) and criminal liability (before a criminal court) can both arise from the same conduct, serving different purposes through different processes.

Under Section 89, the punishment for a first offence of causing a false or misleading advertisement prejudicial to consumers is

Explanation. Section 89 prescribes imprisonment up to two years and a fine up to ten lakh rupees for a first offence.

Under Section 89, what is the punishment for a subsequent (repeat) offence?

en.inOneMinute: Read the full set here, or use the practice card above to test yourself one question at a time.
en.meaning:
Which chapter of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 introduces the formal mediation mechanism?

Explanation. Chapter V, Sections 74 to 81, introduces the formal statutory mediation mechanism under the 2019 Act.

Under Section 74, where are consumer mediation cells attached?

Explanation. Section 74 requires mediation cells attached to District Commissions, State Commissions, the National Commission, and its regional Benches.

How are mediators selected under Sections 75-76?

Explanation. Mediators are empanelled by the Commission, and for each dispute referred to mediation, one is nominated from that empanelled panel.

What must a mediator disclose under Section 77?

en.meaning:
Which chapter of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 deals with product liability?

Explanation. Chapter VI (Sections 82 to 87) deals with product liability.

Which section lays down the grounds of liability of a product manufacturer?

Explanation. Section 84 lists the grounds on which a product manufacturer is liable.

Which is NOT a ground of manufacturer liability under Section 84?

Explanation. Section 84 covers manufacturing defect, design defect, deviation from specifications, non-conformity with express warranty and inadequate instructions or warnings.

Liability of a product seller (who is not the manufacturer) is dealt with in:

en.meaning:
Under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 and the Rules of 2021 made under section 34, the District Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction where the value of goods/services paid as consideration is

Explanation. Section 34 fixes Rs 1 crore unless the Central Government prescribes another value. The 2021 Rules prescribed up to fifty lakh rupees for the District Commission.

Under the 2021 Rules, the State Commission has pecuniary jurisdiction where the consideration paid is

Explanation. The State Commission's pecuniary jurisdiction covers consideration exceeding fifty lakh rupees but not exceeding two crore rupees.

What is the correct order of appeal under the three-tier Commission structure?

Explanation. The correct appellate chain is District Commission → State Commission → National Commission → Supreme Court.

Besides the opposite party's location and where the cause of action arose, where else may a complaint under the 2019 Act be filed?
